questions.explanation: The correct evolutionary sequence, from most primitive to most advanced among these four organisms, runs: Tilapia zilli (IV, a fish) → Bufo regularis (III, a toad/amphibian) → Agama agama (II, a lizard/reptile) → Rattus rattus (I, a rat/mammal) — matching option D.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: The main function of the caudal fin in Tilapia is to

options.D: enable it to float in water

questions.explanation: The caudal (tail) fin's primary role in fish is to generate the powerful thrust that propels the fish forward through the water, via side-to-side sweeping movements — steering and balance are more the roles of the paired and median fins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: In lizards, the lowering of the gular fold is used to
questions.explanation: Lowering the gular fold (throat flap) as a visible display is a courtship behaviour in lizards, used specifically to attract mates, distinct from behaviours like raising a nuchal crest, which is more associated with territorial displays or intimidation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: An example of a fish that aestivates is
questions.explanation: The lungfish is well known for its ability to aestivate — surviving periods when its pond or water body dries up by burrowing into mud and breathing air using its lung-like swim bladder until water returns — a survival strategy not shared by sharks, ordinary catfish, or croakers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: Which of the following is used mainly for balancing in fish?
questions.explanation: As covered earlier, the paired pectoral fins play the primary role in balancing and fine steering control, working alongside the pelvic fins, while the caudal fin mainly powers forward movement and the dorsal/anal fins resist rolling.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: The most important characteristic that makes reptiles conquer terrestrial habitats is the possession of
questions.explanation: The amniotic egg — a shelled egg containing its own internal fluid-filled sac (amnion) that protects the developing embryo and prevents it from drying out — was the critical evolutionary innovation that freed reptiles from needing to return to water to reproduce, enabling their full conquest of terrestrial habitats.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: The first terrestrial vertebrates evolved from
questions.explanation: The first vertebrates to make the transition onto land — the amphibians — themselves evolved from earlier fish (Pisces) ancestors, making Pisces the ultimate evolutionary origin of terrestrial vertebrate life.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: The feature that makes locomotion in water easy for fish is the
questions.explanation: As established earlier, a fish's streamlined (fusiform) body shape is the key adaptation that minimizes water resistance and allows for efficient, energy-saving movement through water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: With respect to their decreasing dependence on aquatic conditions for reproduction, which of the following is the correct arrangement of the animals represented?
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, the animals are arranged from most dependent on water for reproduction (such as a fish) to least dependent (such as a fully terrestrial reptile or bird), matching the sequence IV, III, II, and I as shown in the source text.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: Which of the animals represents the oldest creatures in terms of evolutionary history?
questions.explanation: Consistent with the established evolutionary trend from aquatic to terrestrial vertebrates, the organism labelled IV (representing a fish) is the oldest, most primitive lineage among those shown in the diagram.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: The function of the red head in male Agama lizards is to

options.A: attract female lizards for mating purposes
options.B: warn predators of the distastefulness of the animal
options.C: conceal and camouflage the animal from predators
options.D: scale other males from the territory

questions.explanation: The vivid red head coloration displayed by male Agama lizards during the breeding season functions as a visual signal specifically to attract females for mating, a form of sexual display rather than camouflage or warning coloration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: The basking of Agama lizards in the sun is to

options.A: change the colour of their body
options.B: raise their body temperature to become active

questions.explanation: Being ectothermic (cold-blooded), Agama lizards rely on external heat sources, such as basking in direct sunlight, to raise their body temperature to a level that allows for normal activity and metabolism, since they cannot generate sufficient body heat internally.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subcategory: CLASSIFICATION VI — VERTEBRATES I: PISCES, AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES
questions.question: An example of a poikilothermic organism is a
questions.explanation: The lizard is poikilothermic (cold-blooded), its body temperature varying with the environment. Rabbits and birds are homoiothermic (warm-blooded), and while a cockroach is technically also an ectotherm, in the context of this vertebrate-focused topic, the lizard is the clearly intended and correct example of poikilothermy among vertebrates.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2. The process represented by the above equation is
questions.explanation: This equation — carbon dioxide and water combining, using light energy, to form glucose and oxygen — is the overall summary equation of photosynthesis, the process by which green plants manufacture their own food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The oxygen given off during the process is derived from
questions.explanation: During the light-dependent stage of photosynthesis, water molecules are split apart (photolysis) into hydrogen and oxygen; this released oxygen is the gas given off as a by-product, not the oxygen from carbon dioxide as might be assumed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these elements is required by plants in small quantities only?
questions.explanation: Boron is a micronutrient (trace element), needed by plants only in very minute amounts for processes like pigment and enzyme formation. Nitrogen, phosphorus, magnesium, and potassium, by contrast, are all macronutrients, required in much larger quantities.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these is a direct photosynthetic product?
questions.explanation: Glucose is the direct, immediate sugar product formed at the end of the photosynthetic pathway; starch, fats, proteins, and other substances are all subsequently synthesized or converted from this initial glucose product.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An organism which lives on the remains of a dead plant is
questions.explanation: An organism that feeds on dead and decaying organic matter (such as a dead plant) is, by definition, a saprophyte — distinct from parasites (which feed on a living host) or commensals/symbionts (which involve living partnerships).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the substances listed below is a trace element for plants?
questions.explanation: Copper is a micronutrient (trace element) required by plants only in tiny amounts, unlike potassium and phosphate/nitrate (forms of phosphorus and nitrogen), which are needed in much larger, macronutrient quantities. (Sodium is not a standard required plant nutrient at all.)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A sugar solution was boiled with Fehling's solutions A and B and the colour remained blue. The sugar tested was
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar, so it does not react with Fehling's solution to produce the characteristic colour change from blue to brick-red — the solution stays blue. Glucose, maltose, fructose, and lactose are all reducing sugars and would have given a positive (colour-changing) result.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Alkaline pyrogallol was used in an experiment. That experiment must have been connected with
questions.explanation: Alkaline pyrogallol has a strong affinity for absorbing oxygen gas — a property specifically exploited in photosynthesis experiments to demonstrate that oxygen (a by-product of photosynthesis) has been produced and needs to be absorbed/measured.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The element nitrogen is utilized in
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is a key building-block element specifically required for forming amino acids (and consequently proteins), as well as nitrogenous bases and chlorophyll — but it is not a component of glucose or ATP's core structure, nor a direct requirement of the photosynthetic light/dark reactions themselves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Magnesium is utilized in the formation of
questions.explanation: Magnesium is the central metal atom at the core of the chlorophyll molecule, making it essential specifically for chlorophyll formation, unlike ATP, glucose, amino acids, or fats, whose core structures do not require magnesium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In testing for glucose, the necessary reagent and the condition under which the reagent reacts best are

options.C: Fehling's reagent in acid medium, heated
options.E: Fehling's reagent in neutral or alkaline medium, boiled

questions.explanation: Fehling's test for reducing sugars like glucose requires the solution to be heated (boiled) in a neutral or alkaline medium in order for the characteristic colour change (blue to brick-red) to occur — testing in an acidic medium or without heating would not give a reliable positive result.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A green plant growing in a compost pit is feeding

options.E: in none of the above ways

questions.explanation: Because it is a green plant, it still manufactures its own food by photosynthesis (holophytic/autotrophic nutrition) — simply being rooted in a nutrient-rich compost pit does not change its fundamentally autotrophic mode of nutrition to saprophytic feeding, which requires absorbing organic matter directly (as fungi do).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mushroom is an organism which feeds
questions.explanation: A mushroom (a type of fungus) typically obtains its nutrients by feeding saprophytically — secreting digestive enzymes onto dead organic matter and absorbing the digested products — rather than through any of the other listed nutritional modes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If Benedict's solution gives a positive result in a food test, the food contains
questions.explanation: Benedict's solution is specifically used to test for reducing sugars; a positive result (colour change to green, yellow, orange, or brick-red depending on concentration) confirms the presence of a reducing sugar in the food sample.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The deficiency of Vitamin D leads to
questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency specifically causes rickets in children (or osteomalacia in adults) — a condition of weak, poorly mineralized bones — distinct from scurvy (vitamin C deficiency), pellagra (niacin/B3 deficiency), or beriberi (vitamin B1 deficiency).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these substances is likely to be deficient in the diet of a person having goitre?
questions.explanation: Goitre (an enlarged thyroid gland) results specifically from a deficiency of iodine, which is essential for the production of thyroid hormones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Some of the major elements required by plants are
questions.explanation: Potassium, nitrogen, phosphorus, and calcium are all genuine major (macro-) nutrients required by plants in comparatively large amounts. (Note: sodium is not actually a standard essential plant nutrient, so its inclusion here is a simplification in the original question, but it remains the best-fitting option among those given, since the other options each mix in a genuine trace element — molybdenum, silicon, or cadmium — among the major elements, making them clearly incorrect.)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Kwashiorkor is caused by severe deficiency of
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is a well-known protein-energy malnutrition disorder caused specifically by a severe deficiency of dietary protein, typically seen in children who are weaned early and then fed a starchy, protein-poor diet.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs are the products of sucrose hydrolysis?
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide made of one glucose unit and one fructose unit joined together; hydrolysis (breaking this bond with water) yields exactly these two monosaccharides, glucose and fructose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If an organic compound has its Hydrogen:Oxygen ratio as 2:1, it is likely to be
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are characteristically defined by having their hydrogen and oxygen atoms present in the same ratio as in water (2:1), reflected in the general formula Cx(H2O)y — a signature not shared by proteins, fats, or amino acids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following elements are necessary for the formation of chlorophyll in a plant?
questions.explanation: Magnesium sits at the very core of the chlorophyll molecule, and iron, while not part of the molecule's structure, is required as a catalyst in the chlorophyll synthesis pathway — making magnesium and iron together the correct pairing of elements essential to chlorophyll formation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true of insectivorous plants?

options.A: They obtain part of their food by trapping and feeding on insects
options.B: They attract insects simply because of pollination
options.C: They can grow in soils poor in nitrogenous salts
options.D: They can supplement the nitrogen supply by feeding on insects
options.E: Examples include butterworts, sundews and pitcher plants

questions.explanation: Insectivorous (carnivorous) plants attract and trap insects specifically to digest them as a nutrient (particularly nitrogen) source — not merely for pollination purposes, making option B the false statement. They genuinely do grow in nitrogen-poor soils, supplement nitrogen by digesting insects, and butterworts, sundews, and pitcher plants are all real examples.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A mixture of mercurous and mercuric nitrates is added to a food substance. A white precipitate is formed which on gentle heating turns red. The food substance is
questions.explanation: This colour-change reaction (white precipitate turning red/pink on heating) is characteristic of Millon's test for protein, in which mercury-based reagents react specifically with tyrosine residues found in most proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a Biuret test, some protein was mixed with sodium hydroxide solution. Which of the following chemicals should be added to the mixture for a positive result?
questions.explanation: The Biuret test for protein requires adding dilute copper sulphate solution to an alkaline (sodium hydroxide-containing) sample; a positive result shows as a violet/purple colour change, caused by the copper ions reacting with peptide bonds in the protein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fehling's solution will readily change colour from blue to a reddish colour when it is

options.A: mixed with sugar solution in the cold
options.C: mixed with reducing sugar in the cold
options.D: warmed or heated with a complex solution
options.E: warmed with a solution of reducing sugar

questions.explanation: A positive Fehling's test specifically requires both the presence of a reducing sugar and heating (warming) the mixture — simply mixing in the cold, or heating the reagent alone without a reducing sugar present, will not produce the colour change.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A food substance which produces red colouration with Sudan III contains
questions.explanation: Sudan III is a fat-soluble dye specifically used to test for the presence of fats and oils; a positive test shows as a distinct red (or red-stained) colouration/layer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If calcium is deficient in food this may cause
questions.explanation: Calcium deficiency primarily impairs healthy bone and tooth formation, resulting in retarded growth (as well as weak, stunted development), rather than the other listed conditions, which are linked to different specific nutrient deficiencies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A young plant showing yellow leaves is likely to be deficient in
questions.explanation: Magnesium is a core component of chlorophyll, so a deficiency directly impairs chlorophyll production, causing the yellowing of leaves (chlorosis) characteristic of magnesium-deficient plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Oxygen liberated during photosynthesis has been demonstrated to come from
questions.explanation: As established earlier, isotope-labelling experiments have confirmed that the oxygen released during photosynthesis originates from the splitting (photolysis) of water molecules, not from carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these is a trace element?
questions.explanation: Copper is a micronutrient (trace element), required by living organisms only in very small quantities, unlike iron, calcium, and sulphur, all of which (in this context) are needed in comparatively larger amounts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The main organic substances found in the human body are
questions.explanation: The three primary classes of organic (carbon-based) compounds that make up the bulk of the human body's biochemical composition are carbohydrates, fats, and proteins. Salts, being inorganic, do not belong in a list of "organic substances."

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following elements is essential for the formation of haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Iron is a core structural component of the haem group within haemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells, making it essential for haemoglobin formation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The severe deficiency of vitamin C leads to
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency specifically causes scurvy, characterized by bleeding gums, joint pain, and poor wound healing, distinct from kwashiorkor (protein deficiency), beriberi (vitamin B1 deficiency), or pellagra (niacin/B3 deficiency).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In addition to the high calories derived from fats and oils, they are
questions.explanation: Beyond their major role as a concentrated, long-term energy source, fats and oils also serve a valuable secondary function as insulation, helping to conserve body heat and protect against cold.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The extract from a food substance reacting with sodium hydroxide and copper sulphate solutions will produce violet to purple coloration if
questions.explanation: As established in the earlier Biuret test question, this specific combination of reagents (sodium hydroxide plus dilute copper sulphate) producing a violet/purple colour is the classic positive indicator for the presence of protein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In demonstrating the importance of mineral elements in plants, the culture bottle must be darkened to

options.A: prevent algal growth in culture solution

questions.explanation: In a mineral nutrient (water culture) experiment, the culture solution bottle is darkened specifically to prevent light from reaching the nutrient solution, which would otherwise encourage unwanted algal growth that could interfere with the plant's own uptake of the mineral nutrients being tested.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vitamin which is important in the formation of the retina pigments is
questions.explanation: Vitamin A (retinol, named directly after its role) is essential for forming the light-sensitive pigments in the retina, particularly rhodopsin, which is critical for vision, especially in low light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the standard experiment to show that oxygen is given off during photosynthesis, sodium bicarbonate is used to

options.B: supply mineral salts to water plant

questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate dissolved in the water of a photosynthesis demonstration set-up (e.g. with a submerged aquatic plant like Elodea) decomposes to release carbon dioxide, ensuring an adequate CO2 supply so the plant can photosynthesize actively and produce a measurable stream of oxygen bubbles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If a healthy potted plant is continuously kept in dim light, the rate of photosynthesis is otherwise faster than respiration in bright light. Which of the following is true when kept in dim light?

options.A: the rate of respiration may equal that of photosynthesis
options.B: more carbon dioxide and water are taken in
options.D: the volume of oxygen released increases

questions.explanation: In dim light, the rate of photosynthesis slows down considerably (since photosynthesis is otherwise faster than respiration in bright light), to the point where it may drop to roughly match the plant's constant, ongoing rate of respiration — this balance point is known as the light compensation point.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The seedlings in a rice field were found to have thin lanky growth with reddish leaves and poor root development. This is because the soil lacks
questions.explanation: Phosphorus deficiency in plants classically produces exactly this combination of symptoms: thin, lanky (stunted but elongated) growth, a reddish or purplish leaf discoloration, and poor root development, since phosphorus is vital for root growth and general energy transfer in the plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mode of nutrition in which digestion is extracellular is
questions.explanation: Saprophytic organisms (like fungi) digest their food externally, secreting digestive enzymes onto the organic material outside their own bodies (extracellular digestion) before absorbing the already-digested nutrients, unlike holozoic organisms, which typically digest food internally within their bodies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The first step in the process of photosynthesis is the
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis begins when light energy is absorbed and "activates" (excites) the chlorophyll molecule, which is the essential first step that then drives all the subsequent reactions, including the splitting of water (photolysis) and eventually the fixation of carbon dioxide into sugar.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following food substances will produce a brick-red colour when warmed with Benedict's solution?
questions.explanation: Both glucose and maltose are reducing sugars and would technically give a positive Benedict's test; however, glucose is the standard, most direct reducing sugar example that reliably produces the classic brick-red colour, whereas starch and egg white (protein) are non-reducing/non-sugar substances and would not react this way.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Etiolation is caused by the influence of
questions.explanation: Etiolation — the pale, thin, and elongated growth of a plant — is caused specifically by a lack of adequate light, which prevents normal chlorophyll development and causes the plant to grow abnormally toward any available light source.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is formed immediately after the first product of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Once glucose (the first, direct product of photosynthesis) is formed, it is very rapidly converted into starch for storage in most plants — making starch the substance formed immediately following the initial glucose product.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The element common to protein, carbohydrate and lipid is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen (along with carbon and oxygen) is present in all three major organic food classes — carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins — whereas nitrogen, sulphur, and phosphorus are found only in some of these groups (e.g. nitrogen is characteristic of proteins but not typically of carbohydrates).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: 5cm³ dilute sodium hydroxide solution and 5cm³ one percent copper sulphate solution are added to a solution of food specimen. The purple colour which is observed shows the presence of
questions.explanation: As established in earlier related questions, this exact combination of reagents producing a purple/violet colour change is the standard positive Biuret test result for protein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Interveinal chlorosis is normally associated with the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Interveinal chlorosis (yellowing specifically between the leaf veins, while the veins themselves remain green) is a classic symptom of magnesium deficiency, since magnesium is central to chlorophyll but is mobile within the plant and gets redistributed away from older tissue first, leaving a distinctive veined pattern.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Osmic acid boiled with a solution of food substance gave a black precipitate. This indicated the presence of
questions.explanation: Osmic acid (osmium tetroxide) has a strong affinity for unsaturated fatty components and reacts with fats and oils to produce a characteristic black precipitate/stain, distinguishing it from tests for proteins, amino acids, or starch.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Carnivorous plants are usually found in areas which are
questions.explanation: Carnivorous (insectivorous) plants have evolved their prey-trapping adaptations specifically because they typically grow in nitrogen-poor (nitrate-deficient) soils, and digesting captured insects provides them with a valuable supplementary nitrogen source that the soil cannot.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Green plants are distinguished from other living organisms by their ability to
questions.explanation: The single most defining characteristic that sets green plants apart from most other living organisms is their autotrophic ability to manufacture their own food through photosynthesis, rather than needing to consume other organisms for nutrition.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The failure of transport and respiratory systems in plants, as well as the presence of reddish colour in stems and leaves, results from the deficiency of
questions.explanation: As noted earlier, phosphorus deficiency classically produces reddish/purplish discoloration in stems and leaves, alongside impaired energy transfer processes that are essential to healthy plant transport and metabolic (respiratory) function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a drought situation, plants suffer from water stress which could result in
questions.explanation: Water stress from drought conditions generally slows down and impairs a plant's normal biochemical processes (including photosynthesis and general metabolism), rather than enhancing chemical or microbial activity, or specifically affecting phototropic responses.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: 2H2O → 2H+ + O2(g). The equation above represents a part stage of photosynthesis. Which of the following must be present for this reaction to occur?
questions.explanation: This equation represents the photolysis (light-driven splitting) of water, which specifically requires both light energy and activated chlorophyll to occur — carbon dioxide is not involved at this particular stage (it becomes relevant later, in the dark/carbon-fixation reactions).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In an experiment to investigate the effect of nitrogen on the growth of plants, the substrate should be a medium of
questions.explanation: To isolate and test the specific effect of nitrogen on plant growth, the growing substrate must otherwise be nutrient-free (so any observed effect can be attributed only to the nitrogen being tested) — washed sand fits this requirement, since natural soil, cow dung, or sawdust would already contain unknown amounts of nitrogen and other nutrients that would confound the experiment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which vitamin plays an important role in blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is specifically required for the synthesis of certain blood-clotting factors in the liver; its deficiency leads to prolonged bleeding or haemorrhage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Trace elements are required by plants mainly for the
questions.explanation: Trace elements (micronutrients) such as iron, manganese, and boron are primarily needed by plants in tiny amounts to support the formation of specific pigments (like chlorophyll) and to activate or form various enzymes, rather than serving as bulk structural or energy-storage materials themselves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A food substance was treated with a few drops of Sudan III solution and a red coloration was obtained. The food contained
questions.explanation: As established earlier, a red colouration with Sudan III solution is the classic positive test result confirming the presence of fat (or oil) in a food sample.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The element that is essential for the coagulation of blood is
questions.explanation: Calcium ions play a critical role as a cofactor in the blood clotting cascade, making calcium essential for proper blood coagulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The manufacture of carbohydrates by plants takes place only in
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate manufacture via photosynthesis can only occur in parts of the plant containing chlorophyll (chlorophyllous parts) — this includes green leaves and green stems alike, so restricting the answer to just "leaves" or "green stems" alone would be too narrow; "chlorophyllous parts" is the most technically accurate and complete answer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a water culture experiment, a plant showed poor growth and yellowing of the leaves. These may be due to deficiency of
questions.explanation: As established earlier, magnesium deficiency (given its central role in chlorophyll) is the classic cause of yellowing leaves (chlorosis) combined with generally poor plant growth in a controlled water culture (hydroponic) experiment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Million's test, when the reagent is added to a protein food item, a white precipitate is produced which turns
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the defining feature of a positive Millon's test is the initial white precipitate turning red (or pink) specifically upon gentle heating, confirming the presence of protein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The dark reaction of photosynthesis involves

options.A: fixation of carbon(IV) oxide to give a six-carbon compound
options.B: fixation of carbon(IV) oxide with the help of oxygen
options.C: use of carbon(IV) oxide to produce glucose using ATP
options.D: the fixation of carbon(IV) oxide on chlorophyll using hydrogen

questions.explanation: The dark reaction (Calvin cycle) of photosynthesis involves fixing carbon dioxide onto a starting five-carbon acceptor molecule, ultimately producing six-carbon sugar compounds through a series of enzyme-driven steps using the ATP and NADPH generated earlier in the light reaction — matching option A's description most closely.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The modes of nutrition in Nitrobacter, Ascaris and Homo sapiens respectively are
questions.explanation: Nitrobacter is a chemosynthetic bacterium (deriving energy by oxidizing inorganic nitrogen compounds), Ascaris is a parasitic roundworm, and Homo sapiens (humans) exhibit holozoic nutrition (ingesting and internally digesting solid food) — matching option B exactly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The richest sources of vitamin A are
questions.explanation: Palm oil and carrots are both particularly rich sources of vitamin A precursors (carotenoids, especially beta-carotene), making them a well-matched pair among the options given.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Yellowing of leaves is a symptom associated with deficiency of
questions.explanation: Deficiencies in magnesium, nitrogen, and iron are all well-documented, independent causes of yellowing (chlorosis) in plant leaves — each affects chlorophyll production or general growth in ways that manifest visibly as leaf yellowing, more consistently than the other listed combinations.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The production of violet colouration, when dilute NaOH solution is added to a solution of food substance, followed by drops of 1% CuSO4 solution while making, indicates the presence of
questions.explanation: As established repeatedly in this topic, this specific reagent sequence (dilute sodium hydroxide followed by dilute copper sulphate) producing a violet colouration is the classic positive Biuret test for protein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The greatest amount of energy will be obtained by the oxidation of 100kg of
questions.explanation: Butter (a fat) yields roughly twice as much energy per unit mass as an equivalent mass of carbohydrate (like sugar or biscuits) or protein (like meat), since fats/oils are the most energy-dense of the major food classes — making 100kg of butter the option yielding the greatest amount of energy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mode of feeding in Amoeba and Hydra is
questions.explanation: Both Amoeba and Hydra obtain their nutrition by ingesting and digesting other organisms (a form of heterotrophic, specifically holozoic, nutrition), unlike autotrophic/holophytic organisms, which manufacture their own food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A seedling grown in the dark is likely to be
questions.explanation: As covered earlier, a seedling deprived of light develops the classic pale, thin, and abnormally elongated growth pattern known as etiolation, as it stretches in search of a light source.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When specimen X is mixed with a few drops of iodine solution, the appearance of a blue-black colour confirms that X is
questions.explanation: A blue-black colour change with iodine solution is the classic, specific test result confirming the presence of starch — none of the sugars listed (galactose, sucrose, glucose) give this particular colour reaction with iodine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the experiment?

options.A: The flask must be of the conical type
options.B: Caustic soda can be replaced with distilled water
options.C: The enclosed leaf will lose its green colour
options.D: The leaves outside the flask serve as control

questions.explanation: In this classic experiment, the leaves left outside the enclosed flask are deliberately used as the control group for comparison, since they are exposed to normal atmospheric carbon dioxide, while the enclosed leaf has its carbon dioxide supply removed by the caustic soda.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The experimental set-up can be used to demonstrate that

options.C: photosynthesis occurs in the leaves of plants
options.D: carbon(IV) oxide is necessary for photosynthesis

questions.explanation: Since the caustic soda in the flask absorbs and removes carbon dioxide from the air around the enclosed leaf, this set-up is specifically designed to demonstrate that carbon dioxide is a necessary requirement for photosynthesis (the enclosed leaf, lacking CO2, will fail to produce starch, unlike the control leaves outside).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The capture and digestion of insects by a pitcher plant is a special form of nutrition termed
questions.explanation: Although a pitcher plant is still photosynthetic, the additional capturing and digesting of insects for extra nutrients represents a heterotrophic supplement to its nutrition — this specific trapping/digesting behaviour is not classified as autotrophic, chemosynthetic, or saprophytic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A person that is obese must avoid meals containing
questions.explanation: Margarine and butter are concentrated sources of fat, the most energy-dense food class — an obese individual seeking to reduce excess calorie/fat intake would specifically need to avoid or limit such high-fat foods more than the comparatively lower-fat options listed (fruits, legumes/protein, or starchy staples).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The dark reaction of photosynthesis involves the

options.A: reduction of carbon(IV) oxide to organic compounds
options.B: release of oxygen and the splitting of water
options.C: photolysis of water and the production of starch
options.D: splitting of water into hydrogen ions

questions.explanation: The dark reaction is specifically where carbon dioxide is fixed and then chemically reduced (using the ATP and NADPH generated in the light reaction) into organic compounds such as sugars — the splitting of water and release of oxygen are light reaction processes, not dark reaction ones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: All living cells require water because it

options.A: is a medium for all metabolic reactions
options.B: is a medium that neutralizes acids in cells
options.C: is the main source of energy for the cells
options.D: prevents the development of diseases in cells

questions.explanation: Water serves as the universal solvent and medium within which essentially all of a cell's metabolic (biochemical) reactions take place — this fundamental role is why water is indispensable to every living cell, far more broadly important than any narrower function like acid neutralization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Night-blindness results from a deficiency of
questions.explanation: As established earlier, vitamin A is essential for forming the retinal pigments needed for vision, particularly in low-light conditions — its deficiency specifically causes night-blindness, progressing to more severe vision problems if prolonged.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The photosynthetic pigments include
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll (the main pigment) and carotenoids (accessory pigments, including carotenes and xanthophylls) together make up the key light-absorbing pigments involved in photosynthesis — cytochromes, melanin, and haemoglobin all serve entirely different biological roles unrelated to capturing light for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Stunted growth and poor root development are a result of a deficiency in
questions.explanation: As established earlier, phosphorus deficiency classically produces stunted growth together with poor root development, since phosphorus plays a central role in energy transfer and cell division processes vital to healthy root growth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Insectivorous plants trap and kill their prey to derive
questions.explanation: As established earlier, insectivorous plants specifically supplement their nitrogen intake (which is often scarce in the nutrient-poor soils they inhabit) by capturing and digesting insects, rather than targeting these other minerals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a carnivorous plant?
questions.explanation: The bladderwort is a genuine carnivorous plant, equipped with small bladder-like traps that capture tiny aquatic organisms. Hydra is an animal (not a plant), while yeast and Spirogyra are non-carnivorous fungi/algae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is lacking in the diet of a person with kwashiorkor?
questions.explanation: As established earlier, kwashiorkor is specifically a protein-deficiency disorder, resulting from a diet severely lacking in adequate dietary protein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When a mixture of a food substance and Benedict's solution was warmed, the solution changed from blue to brick-red. This indicates the presence of
questions.explanation: As established repeatedly throughout this topic, a colour change from blue to brick-red upon warming with Benedict's solution is the definitive positive test result for a reducing sugar.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Chemosynthetic organisms are capable of manufacturing their food from simple inorganic substances through the process of
questions.explanation: Chemosynthetic organisms (such as nitrifying bacteria) manufacture their food by oxidizing simple inorganic substances (such as ammonia or nitrites), releasing energy that is then used to fix carbon dioxide into organic compounds — this oxidation process is the defining feature of chemosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: (I) Parasitism — Sendew (II) Autotrophism — Amoeba (III) Saprophytism — Alga (IV) Heterotrophism — Agama. Which of the above modes of nutrition is correctly matched with the organism that exhibits it?
questions.explanation: Agama (a lizard) genuinely exhibits heterotrophic nutrition (feeding on other organisms), making pairing IV the only correctly matched combination — Sundew is actually carnivorous/autotrophic (not simply parasitic), Amoeba is heterotrophic (not autotrophic), and algae are autotrophic/photosynthetic (not saprophytic).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In plants, which of the following is required in minute quantities for growth?
questions.explanation: As established earlier, copper is a micronutrient (trace element), needed by plants only in very small quantities for growth, distinct from macronutrients like potassium and phosphorus, which are required in much larger amounts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following organisms is both parasitic and autotrophic?
questions.explanation: Loranthus (a mistletoe) is a partial (hemi-) parasitic plant — it taps into its host's xylem to obtain water and minerals (a parasitic behaviour), while still retaining its own chlorophyll and manufacturing some of its own food by photosynthesis (an autotrophic behaviour), uniquely combining both modes of nutrition among these options.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a polysaccharide?
questions.explanation: Cellulose is a true polysaccharide, made of many linked glucose units. Glucose is a monosaccharide, while sucrose and maltose are disaccharides (made of only two linked sugar units each).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During the manufacture of food by plants, which of the following organisms use energy from the sun?
questions.explanation: Anabaena is a photosynthetic cyanobacterium (blue-green alga), meaning it uses light energy from the sun to manufacture its food, unlike sulphur bacteria, Nitrosomonas, and Nitrobacter, which are all chemosynthetic organisms that derive their energy instead from oxidizing inorganic chemical compounds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plants that have special devices for trapping and digesting insects are
questions.explanation: Plants equipped with specialized structures for capturing and digesting insects (such as sundews, pitcher plants, and bladderworts) are classified as carnivorous (insectivorous) plants — a distinct category from symbiotic, parasitic, or saprophytic organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When proteins are broken down they also provide
questions.explanation: The final products of protein digestion (hydrolysis) are amino acids, the individual building-block units that made up the original protein chain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mammalian stomach can carry out a number of processes except
questions.explanation: Trypsin is produced by the pancreas, not the stomach. The stomach genuinely does secrete hydrochloric acid and gastric juice (containing pepsin and rennin), churns food mechanically, and can absorb only very limited substances (glucose absorption mainly occurs later, in the small intestine, though minimal absorption in the stomach itself is not its primary role).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these is the terminal portion of the alimentary canal of a mammal?
questions.explanation: The rectum is the final section of the alimentary canal, immediately preceding the anus, where faecal waste is temporarily stored before elimination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these is not an enzyme?
questions.explanation: Gastrin is a hormone (produced by the stomach lining, stimulating acid secretion), not an enzyme — pepsin, amylase, chymotrypsin, and trypsin are all genuine digestive enzymes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The digestive enzyme that coagulates protein in milk is
questions.explanation: Renin (rennin) specifically curdles milk by converting soluble caseinogen protein into insoluble casein, which then gets broken down further by pepsin — this specific curdling action is unique to renin among the enzymes listed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The arrangements below are steps in protein digestion. Which is the correct sequence? (a) polypeptides (b) protein (c) amino acids (d) peptones
questions.explanation: Protein digestion proceeds through progressively smaller fragments: the whole protein (b) is first broken into peptones (d), then into polypeptides (a), and finally into individual amino acids (c) — giving the correct sequence b→d→a→c.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following organs produces bile?
questions.explanation: Bile is produced by the liver, then stored and concentrated in the gall bladder (not produced there), before being released into the duodenum when needed for fat digestion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following food substances is digested in the stomach?
questions.explanation: The stomach's digestive enzymes (pepsin and rennin) act specifically on proteins; carbohydrate digestion (started by salivary ptyalin) is actually paused in the acidic stomach environment, and fat digestion mainly occurs later in the small intestine, not the stomach.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is the dental formula of man?
questions.explanation: The correct human dental formula is 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars, and 3 molars per quadrant (i2/2, c1/1, pm2/2, m3/3), giving a total of 32 teeth — matching option E exactly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The kind of teeth used for tearing food materials is the
questions.explanation: The canine teeth, being pointed and prominent, are specifically adapted for gripping and tearing flesh or food materials, distinct from incisors (cutting/nibbling) or premolars/molars (grinding/crushing).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Milk protein is hydrolysed by
questions.explanation: As established earlier, renin (rennin) is the specific enzyme responsible for curdling (coagulating) milk protein (caseinogen), the first step before pepsin further hydrolyses the resulting casein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: All the following are digestive enzymes except
questions.explanation: Bile is not an enzyme at all — it is a fluid secretion that physically emulsifies fats (breaking them into smaller droplets) to aid enzymatic digestion, but it contains no digestive enzymes itself, unlike lipase, maltase, pepsin, and ptyalin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The correct route for a piece of bread eaten by a mammal is
questions.explanation: Although this option's listed order technically omits an explicit separate mention of the duodenum (implicitly included within "ileum" as part of the small intestine sequence), it is the only option that keeps the organs in a broadly correct anatomical order: mouth → oesophagus → stomach → small intestine (duodenum/ileum) → rectum, unlike the other options, which incorrectly reorder the stomach, oesophagus, or duodenum out of sequence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the enzyme reaction starch → sugar (via amylase), starch is referred to as the
questions.explanation: In any enzyme-catalyzed reaction, the starting substance that the enzyme acts upon (here, starch) is called the substrate, while the resulting substance (sugar) is called the product.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If the gall bladder of a man is removed by surgery, which of the following processes will be most seriously affected?
questions.explanation: Since the gall bladder's specific role is to store and release bile (which emulsifies fats to aid their digestion), its removal would most seriously affect the efficient digestion of fats and oils — the liver would still produce bile, but its convenient storage and controlled release would be lost.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mammalian pancreas is involved with the

options.C: digestion of food and regulation of blood sugar
options.D: digestion of hormone and the regulation of blood sugar
options.E: digestion of food, and the production of insulin

questions.explanation: The pancreas has this important dual role: its exocrine function produces digestive enzymes (for food digestion), and its endocrine function produces insulin and glucagon (for regulating blood sugar levels) — matching option C's description of both roles together.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The dental formula i2/1, c1/1, pm2/1, m3/2 = 42 represents that of a
questions.explanation: A total tooth count of 42, with this particular formula pattern (including a relatively larger number of premolars and molars), is characteristic of the dog, a carnivore — distinctly different from man's 32-tooth formula, or a rabbit's/sheep's herbivore-adapted formula.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the dentition of man is INCORRECT?

options.C: the same number of teeth on upper and lower jaws

questions.explanation: Man has a total of 12 molars (3 molars × 2 sides × 2 jaws = 12), not just six, making this the incorrect statement. Man genuinely has more molars (12) than incisors (8), no diastema, an equal tooth count on both jaws, and a total of 32 teeth overall.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mouth parts of the housefly are adapted for
questions.explanation: The housefly digests solid food externally by regurgitating saliva onto it, then uses its spongy, sponge-like proboscis to lap and soak up (sponge) the resulting liquefied food — a feeding method distinct from biting/chewing insects or piercing-sucking insects like mosquitoes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true of enzymes? They
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins, and like all proteins, they are denatured (permanently lose their functional shape and activity) by high temperatures — making the claim that they "can withstand high temperatures" the false statement. Enzymes genuinely can require cofactors, and their activity is indeed sensitive to pH (hydrogen ion concentration).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Pepsin is a digestive enzyme which breaks

options.D: fats into glycerol and fatty acids

questions.explanation: Pepsin is a protein-digesting (proteolytic) enzyme found in the stomach, specifically breaking down proteins into smaller peptone/polypeptide fragments — it plays no role in digesting carbohydrates, cellulose, fats, or sucrose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The removal of a man's pancreas by surgical operation can affect only the digestion of
questions.explanation: The pancreas produces enzymes for digesting carbohydrates (amylopsin), fats (steapsin/lipase), and proteins (trypsin) — but since some protein digestion can still occur via stomach pepsin, the most directly and exclusively pancreas-dependent digestive processes affected are those of carbohydrates and fats.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The presence of diastema in the jawbone indicates that the mammal lacks the teeth suitable for
questions.explanation: A diastema (a gap in the jaw, typically where canines would normally sit) indicates the animal lacks the canine teeth needed for tearing/gripping flesh — consistent with the jaw structure of herbivores, which have no functional need for tearing teeth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following represents the sequence of protein hydrolysis? (1) Polypeptides (2) Amino acids (3) Proteins (4) Peptones
questions.explanation: As established earlier, protein digestion breaks the whole protein (3) down progressively into peptones (4), then polypeptides (1), and finally amino acids (2) — matching the sequence 3→4→1→2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Partially digested food ready to leave the stomach is referred to as
questions.explanation: The semi-liquid, partially digested food mass that leaves the stomach and enters the duodenum is specifically termed chyme (distinct from "chyle," the term used for the similarly partially digested food ready to leave the duodenum after further digestion).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The three important organs that are situated close to the stomach are
questions.explanation: The gall bladder (embedded in a lobe of the liver near the stomach), the pancreas (nestled in the duodenal loop close by), and the spleen (attached along the stomach's undersurface) are all anatomically positioned close to the stomach, unlike the kidneys, which sit further back in the abdominal cavity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Evidence that a tooth is a living part of the mammalian body can be found within the
questions.explanation: The pulp cavity, located at the centre of the tooth, contains living tissue — including blood vessels and nerves — providing direct evidence that the tooth is a living structure, unlike the enamel or cement, which are hard, largely non-living, mineralized coverings.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following lists of organs is directly involved in nutrition?

options.A: Oesophagus, bronchus, stomach, pancreas and anus
options.B: Spleen, pharynx, duodenum, jejunum and rectum
options.C: Teeth, oesophagus, ileum, lungs and large intestine
options.D: Salivary gland, liver, stomach, villi and colon

questions.explanation: Only option D lists exclusively organs/structures that genuinely play a direct role in nutrition (salivary gland for initial digestion, liver for bile/metabolism, stomach for digestion, villi for absorption, colon for water absorption) — the other options each mix in an unrelated organ (such as the bronchus or lungs, which are respiratory, not digestive).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If an animal has diastema, it would NOT possess
questions.explanation: As established earlier, a diastema is the gap that forms specifically where canine teeth would be, indicating the animal lacks (or has non-functional/absent) canines.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If the gall bladder of a mammal is damaged, which of the following will be most seriously affected?
questions.explanation: As established earlier, damage to the gall bladder (which stores and releases bile for fat emulsification) would most directly impair the efficient digestion of fats and oils.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following will be first digested if ingested at the same time?
questions.explanation: Cooked starch (as found in cooked rice) begins being digested almost immediately in the mouth by the enzyme ptyalin (salivary amylase), giving it a head start compared to proteins (beans, beef) or fats (cod liver oil), which are not digested until later, in the stomach and small intestine respectively.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the structures is the molar?
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, structure 1 corresponds to the molar, the broad, flat-surfaced tooth positioned at the back of the jaw, adapted for grinding food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the function of 3?

options.A: Cutting off large pieces of food

questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, structure 3 corresponds to the canine tooth, whose pointed shape is specifically adapted for seizing and tearing prey.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The pancreatic juice contains the enzymes amylopsin,
questions.explanation: Pancreatic juice contains three main enzyme types: amylopsin (for carbohydrate digestion), steapsin (lipase, for fat digestion), and trypsinogen (the inactive precursor of trypsin, for protein digestion) — matching option C.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The organ which secretes digestive enzymes as well as hormone is the
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the pancreas uniquely combines both digestive enzyme secretion (exocrine function) and hormone secretion — insulin and glucagon (endocrine function).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The villus in the small intestine is significant because it

options.A: increases the surface area for absorption
options.B: increases the surface area for digestion

questions.explanation: The many finger-like villi projecting from the intestinal wall dramatically increase the internal surface area available for absorbing digested nutrients into the bloodstream — their primary significance relates to absorption, not digestion itself.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: One of the accessory organs of the digestive system is the
questions.explanation: The liver is a genuine accessory organ of the digestive system, producing bile that aids fat digestion, even though food does not pass directly through it — the kidney, spleen, and lung are not part of the digestive system at all.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The crown of the mammalian tooth is covered with
questions.explanation: Enamel, the hardest substance in the body, specifically caps and protects the crown (the visible part above the gum) of a mammalian tooth, while cement covers the root region instead.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which enzymes are contained in the pancreatic juice?
questions.explanation: As established earlier, pancreatic juice specifically contains amylase (carbohydrate-digesting), lipase (fat-digesting), and trypsin/trypsinogen (protein-digesting) enzymes, matching option D — ptyalin, pepsin, rennin, and maltase/erepsin belong to other digestive secretions (saliva, gastric juice, or intestinal juice), not pancreatic juice.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The lower jaw is typical of a
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, the specific jaw structure shown (with its particular diastema positioning between a non-functional lower canine and the premolar) is characteristic of a sheep, distinguishing it from the jaw arrangement of a rabbit or the carnivorous dentition of a dog or cat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The end products of the digestion of fats and oils in mammals are
questions.explanation: Fats and oils, being triglycerides, are fully hydrolyzed by lipase into their two component building blocks: fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The dental formula i3, c1, pm4, m3 is that of a
questions.explanation: This particular formula, with its greater number of premolars (4) and prominent canines (1), giving a total of 42 teeth, is characteristic of the dog, a carnivore — quite different from the dental formula of herbivores like goats/rabbits or of man.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The activity of ptyalin is likely to decrease with an increase in the concentration of
questions.explanation: Ptyalin (salivary amylase) functions best in a neutral to slightly alkaline environment, so an increase in acidity (such as when food reaches the stomach) rapidly decreases and eventually halts its enzymatic activity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the stomach nearer the gullet is called the
questions.explanation: The cardiac sphincter (cardia region) is the valve/opening located at the top of the stomach, nearest the oesophagus (gullet), controlling the entry of swallowed food, in contrast to the pyloric sphincter, which is at the opposite (lower, exit) end of the stomach near the duodenum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The group of insects that have mouth parts adapted for both piercing and sucking is
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes, tsetse flies, and aphids all possess specialized needle-like mouthparts adapted for piercing through skin or plant tissue and then sucking up blood or sap — a combination not shared by cockroaches (biting/chewing), houseflies (sponging), moths (sucking only, via proboscis), beetles, or grasshoppers (biting/chewing).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme invertase will hydrolyze sucrose to give
questions.explanation: Invertase specifically breaks down the disaccharide sucrose into its two component monosaccharides, glucose and fructose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The carnassial teeth of a carnivorous animal consist of the

options.A: last upper premolar and the first lower molar
options.B: last upper molar and the last lower molar
options.C: first upper premolar and the first lower molar
options.D: first upper molar and the first lower molar

questions.explanation: In carnivores, the specialized carnassial teeth — adapted with a scissor-like shearing action for cutting through flesh and bone — are specifically the last upper premolar (LUP) and the first lower molar (FLM).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Examples of organisms in which extracellular digestion occurs are
questions.explanation: Rhizopus (a fungus, digesting food externally via secreted enzymes), the housefly (regurgitating saliva onto food before sponging it up), and Hydra (digesting captured prey partly within its gut cavity, effectively outside true cellular boundaries) are all genuine examples of organisms carrying out extracellular digestion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The organ located within the duodenal loop in the mammal is the
questions.explanation: The pancreas is anatomically nestled within the curve (loop) formed by the duodenum, a distinctive positional relationship not shared by the spleen, liver, or gall bladder.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of mammalian digestive system where absorption of nutrients takes place is the
questions.explanation: The ileum (the final and longest section of the small intestine, richly lined with villi) is the primary site where digested nutrients are absorbed into the bloodstream.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An insect with a mandibulate mouth part will obtain its food by
questions.explanation: Mandibulate (mandible-equipped) mouthparts, as found in insects like grasshoppers and cockroaches, are specifically adapted for biting off and chewing solid food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The gall bladder of a mammal has a duct connected to the
questions.explanation: The gall bladder's bile duct connects directly to the duodenum, through which stored bile is released when needed to aid fat digestion in that section of the small intestine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The breakdown of fats and oils into simpler absorbable compounds is catalyzed by the group of enzymes called
questions.explanation: Lipases are the specific class of enzymes responsible for breaking down (hydrolyzing) fats and oils into their absorbable component parts (fatty acids and glycerol).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Rodents gnaw on food with their
questions.explanation: Rodents have characteristically chisel-shaped, continuously growing front incisor teeth, specifically adapted for gnawing on tough food materials.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The pancreas secretes enzymes for the digestion of
questions.explanation: As established throughout this topic, the pancreas secretes enzymes covering all three major food classes: lipase (for fats), trypsin (for proteins), and amylase (for carbohydrates) — vitamins, cellulose, and minerals are not broken down by pancreatic (or any mammalian) digestive enzymes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The order of passage of food in the digestive system is
questions.explanation: Following digestion in the small intestine (ileum), food residue passes into the caecum, then continues through the large intestine (colon), before finally reaching the rectum for elimination — matching the order given in option A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the alimentary system of a bird, the function of teeth is carried out by
questions.explanation: Since birds have no teeth, the muscular, stone-containing gizzard performs the mechanical grinding function that teeth would otherwise carry out, crushing swallowed food into smaller particles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Chewing the cud is an adaptation peculiar to
questions.explanation: "Chewing the cud" (rumination) — regurgitating partially digested food from a specialized multi-chambered stomach for further chewing — is an adaptation specific to ruminants (such as cattle, sheep, and goats), a particular subgroup of herbivores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the alimentary system of a bird where food is ground into small particles is the
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the muscular gizzard, often containing swallowed grit or small stones, is specifically responsible for mechanically grinding a bird's food into smaller particles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the human gut that has an acidic content is the
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the stomach's secretion of hydrochloric acid gives it a characteristically acidic content, unlike the duodenum, ileum, and colon, whose environments are generally more neutral to alkaline.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The conversion of a nutrient into a molecule in the body of a consumer is referred to as
questions.explanation: Assimilation is specifically the process by which absorbed nutrients are converted and incorporated into the body's own molecules and structures, the final step following ingestion, digestion, and absorption.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the test tubes will glucose be detected after complete hydrolysis?
questions.explanation: Cane sugar (sucrose) will only be hydrolyzed into its component sugars (including glucose) when a catalyst — either dilute acid (test tube II) or its specific breaking-down enzyme (test tube III) — is present to speed up the reaction; plain water alone (test tube I) is insufficient to bring about hydrolysis in a reasonable time frame.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme involved in the hydrolysis is
questions.explanation: Sucrase (also called invertase) is the specific enzyme that hydrolyzes sucrose (cane sugar) into glucose and fructose, distinct from maltase (acts on maltose), rennin (curdles milk protein), or erepsin (acts on peptides).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An example of a filter-feeding animal is
questions.explanation: Certain whales (baleen whales) are classic filter feeders, straining vast quantities of small prey (like krill) from seawater using comb-like baleen plates instead of teeth — a feeding method quite different from that of mosquitoes, sharks, or butterflies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A function of the hydrochloric acid produced in the human stomach during digestion is to

options.B: coagulate milk protein and emulsify fats
options.D: break up food into smaller particles

questions.explanation: The strongly acidic environment created by stomach hydrochloric acid halts the activity of ptyalin (salivary amylase), which requires a neutral/alkaline pH to function — hydrochloric acid's other roles include activating pepsin and killing ingested bacteria, but coagulating milk (renin's job) and emulsifying fat (bile's job) are not its functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process in which complex substances are broken down into simpler ones is referred to as
questions.explanation: Catabolism is specifically the breakdown of complex substances into simpler ones (releasing energy in the process, as in digestion and respiration), the opposite of anabolism (building up simpler substances into more complex ones).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme that is present in the saliva is
questions.explanation: Ptyalin (salivary amylase) is the specific enzyme found in saliva, responsible for beginning the digestion of starch into maltose while food is still in the mouth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: i2, c1, pm3, m3. The dental formula above represents that of
questions.explanation: This dental formula's absence of a functional canine (or a canine reduced/aligned with the incisors) alongside a strong emphasis on premolars and molars for grinding is characteristic of a herbivore's dentition, adapted for a plant-based diet rather than tearing flesh.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: One of the functions of the xylem is
questions.explanation: Xylem tissue, being made of thickened, often lignified dead cells, gives significant mechanical strength and support to the stem, in addition to its main role of conducting water — it does not manufacture food, conduct manufactured food (that's phloem's job), reduce water loss, or store sugar.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The cilia in paramecium are used for
questions.explanation: Paramecium's numerous cilia beat rhythmically to propel the organism through water, making locomotion their primary function, alongside a secondary role in directing food particles toward the oral groove (not a primary respiratory, protective, or excretory role).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these skeletons is most appropriate to the cockroach?
questions.explanation: The cockroach, an arthropod, possesses a hard, chitinous exoskeleton covering the outside of its body, which provides both support and protection, unlike vertebrate endoskeletons or the fluid-based hydrostatic skeletons of soft-bodied invertebrates.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these is not associated with the movement of toad, reptile or birds?
questions.explanation: Pecking is a feeding-related action, not a form of locomotion — hopping (toads), flapping/gliding (birds), and general movement patterns of reptiles are all genuine modes of movement, unlike pecking.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these tissues serves the function of support and water conduction?
questions.explanation: Xylem uniquely combines both functions — its lignified, hollow dead cells provide mechanical support to the plant while simultaneously conducting water and dissolved minerals upward, a dual role not matched by parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma (support only), or phloem (food conduction only).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the structures listed below is peculiar to the Axis vertebra?
questions.explanation: The odontoid process (also called the dens) is a distinctive, forward-projecting peg-like structure unique to the axis (the second cervical vertebra), around which the atlas (first cervical vertebra) rotates — the other structures listed are more general features found across multiple vertebrae types.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The joint between the atlas and axis vertebrae allows for

options.B: up and down or nodding movements only

questions.explanation: The atlas-axis joint is specifically a pivot joint, allowing the head to rotate from side to side (as in shaking the head "no") — nodding movements (up and down) instead occur at the separate joint between the skull and the atlas.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Fig. 1, the structure which prevents friction between the bones is
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, part 2 corresponds to the synovial fluid, which lubricates the joint space between two articulating bones, reducing friction during movement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In animals, cilia, flagella, pseudopodia, and chaetae can be used for
questions.explanation: Cilia, flagella, pseudopodia, and chaetae are all structures that different organisms use, in their own specific ways, to achieve movement (locomotion) — swimming, crawling, or gripping the substrate to move forward.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The joint at Y in the fig is
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, the joint labelled Y (typically representing the elbow region) is a hinge joint, allowing movement in essentially one plane (back-and-forth bending), unlike the multi-directional ball-and-socket joint.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The tissue which connects a muscle to a bone is a
questions.explanation: A tendon is specifically the tough connective tissue that attaches a muscle to a bone, enabling the muscle's contraction to pull and move that bone — distinct from a ligament, which connects bone to bone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The thoracic vertebrae of a mammal is characterized by the
questions.explanation: Thoracic vertebrae are specifically distinguished by their long, prominent neural spines, which project upward and backward, providing large attachment surfaces for back muscles and ligaments, unlike the vertebrarterial canal (a cervical vertebra feature).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which vertebra has a projection called odontoid process?
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the odontoid process is a distinctive projecting structure specific to the axis vertebra, around which the atlas pivots to allow head rotation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the parts are used to recognize the bone in the above fig?
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, the combination of parts 1, 3, and 5 together represent the distinguishing structural features (such as the neural spine, transverse process, and centrum shape) needed to correctly identify the specific type of vertebra shown.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Starting from the skull end, the vertebrae are arranged in the following order:

options.A: axis, atlas, cervical, thoracic and lumbar
options.B: atlas, cervical, axis, thoracic and lumbar
options.C: atlas, axis, thoracic, cervical and lumbar
options.D: atlas, axis, cervical, thoracic and lumbar
options.E: atlas, thoracic, cervical, axis and lumbar

questions.explanation: Starting closest to the skull, the correct anatomical sequence of the vertebral column runs: atlas (1st cervical vertebra) → axis (2nd cervical vertebra) → the remaining cervical vertebrae → thoracic vertebrae → lumbar vertebrae, matching option D.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following types of vertebrae occur in equal numbers in the rabbit, rat and man?
questions.explanation: All mammals, regardless of the length or shape of their neck, possess exactly seven cervical vertebrae — a remarkably consistent feature shared equally by rabbits, rats, and man, unlike the variable numbers of thoracic, lumbar, sacral, or caudal (tail) vertebrae between species.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The axial skeleton of a mammal does not include the bones of the
questions.explanation: The axial skeleton comprises the skull, vertebral column (including neck, back, and tail regions), and rib cage/sternum — the limb bones (and their girdles) belong instead to the separate appendicular skeleton.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The appendicular skeleton is made up of the
questions.explanation: The appendicular skeleton consists specifically of the limb bones together with the girdles (pectoral and pelvic) that attach those limbs to the axial skeleton — making "girdles and limbs" the most complete and accurate description among the options.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Two main distinguishing features of the cervical vertebra are the presence of

options.A: short neural spine and vertebrarterial canal

questions.explanation: Cervical vertebrae are specifically distinguished by having a short neural spine along with the vertebrarterial canal (a small opening in the transverse process through which the vertebral artery passes) — a combination of features unique to this region of the vertebral column.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sclerenchyma cells are lignified to
questions.explanation: The deposition of lignin in sclerenchyma cell walls makes them tough and rigid specifically to provide mechanical strength and support to the plant, rather than serving a transport or conduction role (those are functions of xylem and phloem instead).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Parenchyma cells serve as supporting tissue when they
