questions.explanation: When parenchyma cells absorb water and become turgid (firm, swollen with internal pressure against their cell walls), they collectively provide a form of structural support to soft plant tissues — flaccid (water-deficient) parenchyma cells provide no such support.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The lumbar vertebra when compared with a thoracic vertebra has a
questions.explanation: Lumbar vertebrae are specifically characterized by having a noticeably thicker, larger centrum (body) compared with thoracic vertebrae, reflecting the greater weight-bearing demands placed on the lower back.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Muscles are indirectly attached to bones by means of
questions.explanation: As established earlier, tendons are the connective tissue structures that attach muscles to bones, allowing the force of muscle contraction to be transferred to move the skeleton.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following vertebrae lacks a centrum?
questions.explanation: The atlas (first cervical vertebra) is unusual in lacking a true centrum (body) of its own — its centrum has effectively fused onto the axis below it, becoming the axis's distinctive odontoid process instead.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The bone of the neck on which the skull rests is known as the
questions.explanation: The atlas is the topmost cervical vertebra, specifically shaped to support and articulate directly with the base of the skull, allowing nodding movements of the head.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of the vertebrae along the spinal column?

options.A: Axis, atlas, thoracic, lumbar, cervical, sacral
options.B: Atlas, cervical, axis, thoracic, lumbar, sacral
options.C: Atlas, axis, cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral

questions.explanation: As established earlier, the correct vertebral sequence from the skull downward begins with the atlas, then the axis, followed by the remaining cervical vertebrae, then thoracic, lumbar, and finally sacral vertebrae — matching option C.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The phloem parenchyma is sometimes used for
questions.explanation: Phloem parenchyma cells, positioned alongside the actual food-conducting sieve tubes, often serve a secondary role in storing food reserves, rather than support, sieve tube production, or water transport (which are unrelated functions belonging to other tissues).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vertebra illustrated is
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram's distinguishing features (such as a vertebrarterial canal), the vertebra illustrated is identified as a cervical vertebra.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During the bending of the arm, the biceps muscle

options.A: contracts and the triceps muscle relaxes
options.B: relaxes and the triceps muscle contracts

questions.explanation: Bending (flexing) the arm occurs when the biceps muscle contracts while its antagonistic partner, the triceps, correspondingly relaxes — this coordinated, opposing action between antagonistic muscle pairs is how skeletal movement is controlled.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A band of connective tissue linking two bones in a joint is known as
questions.explanation: A ligament is specifically the tough band of connective tissue that links one bone directly to another bone across a joint, providing stability — distinct from a tendon, which links muscle to bone.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The appendicular skeleton is composed of the

options.A: pectoral girdle, pelvic girdle, fore and hind limbs
options.D: lumbar vertebrae, fore and hind limbs

questions.explanation: As established earlier, the appendicular skeleton comprises both girdles (pectoral and pelvic) together with both sets of limbs (fore and hind) — option A captures this complete and accurate composition.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not a function of the mammalian skeleton?
questions.explanation: While the ribs do assist the mechanics of breathing, "respiration" itself (gas exchange) is not a direct function performed by the skeleton — protection (of vital organs), transportation (via limb movement), and support (holding up the body) are the skeleton's genuine core functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The organism that has a hydrostatic skeleton is
questions.explanation: The earthworm relies on a hydrostatic skeleton — fluid-filled body compartments under muscular control, which provide support and enable movement by peristaltic contractions — unlike Tilapia (bony endoskeleton), Hydra (no true skeleton needed given its small size/simplicity), or mosquito larvae (which may have other support structures).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The chitin in the exoskeleton of many arthropods is strengthened by
questions.explanation: In many arthropods, the chitin of the exoskeleton is further hardened and strengthened through the deposition of calcium compounds (such as calcium carbonate), a process called calcification, particularly notable in crustaceans.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the bones is the radius?
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, part IV corresponds to the radius, one of the two long bones of the forearm, positioned alongside the ulna.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The scapula and the ischium are part of the
questions.explanation: Although the scapula (part of the pectoral girdle) and the ischium (part of the pelvic girdle) belong to two different specific girdle structures, both ultimately belong to the broader appendicular skeleton, making this the most complete, correctly encompassing answer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The structure above represents a
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram's characteristic features (such as the vertebrarterial canal), the structure shown represents a cervical vertebra.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The transition from amphibians to mammals involves limbs becoming arranged to support the weight more effectively, requiring modifications in the
questions.explanation: As vertebrates evolved from a sprawling amphibian posture toward more upright, weight-bearing limb postures (as seen progressively in reptiles and mammals), the pectoral and pelvic girdles specifically underwent the key structural modifications needed to more effectively support and transmit body weight through the limbs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hydrostatic skeleton is the type of supporting system found in
questions.explanation: Oligochaetes (such as earthworms) rely on a hydrostatic skeleton (fluid-filled body cavity under muscular control), unlike mammals and reptiles (bony endoskeletons) or arthropods (chitinous exoskeletons).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A unique characteristic of the cervical vertebrae is the process of
questions.explanation: As established repeatedly throughout this topic, the vertebrarterial canal (allowing passage of the vertebral artery) is the specific, defining feature unique to cervical vertebrae, not found in other regions of the vertebral column.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A plant parenchyma cell also acts as a supporting tissue when it
questions.explanation: As established earlier, a parenchyma cell provides supportive rigidity to soft plant tissue specifically when it is turgid (swollen with absorbed water pressing against its cell wall), not when flaccid, crystal-containing, or pigmented.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The axial skeleton is found in the

options.A: skull, ribs, vertebral column and breast bone
options.B: skull, humerus, vertebral column and ribs
options.C: breastbone, clavicle, ribs and vertebral column

questions.explanation: The axial skeleton correctly comprises the skull, vertebral column, ribs, and breastbone (sternum) — the other options each incorrectly include a limb bone (humerus, clavicle, femur, or ulna), which belong instead to the appendicular skeleton.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The two halves of the pelvic girdle are joined together at the
questions.explanation: The two halves of the pelvic girdle meet and are joined together at the front by a specific joint called the pubic symphysis, a slightly movable cartilaginous joint.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The main structure in vertebrates that supports and protects the body is the
questions.explanation: The skeleton, as the overall rigid framework of the body, is the main structure providing both mechanical support and protection for vulnerable internal organs — ligaments, muscles, and joints are all important components that work together with the skeleton, but the skeleton itself is the primary supporting/protective structure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A carbohydrate molecule in the right ventricle of the heart is pumped into the cell of the toe of man. Which of these structures is it unlikely to pass through en-route?
questions.explanation: Blood leaving the right ventricle follows the route: pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → femoral artery → toe. The liver is not on this direct pulmonary-then-systemic circulation pathway to the toe, making it the one structure the blood would not need to pass through.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The hepatic portal vein is characterized by
questions.explanation: A "portal" vein, by definition, both begins and ends in a capillary network — the hepatic portal vein starts as capillaries in the intestinal wall (absorbing digested food) and ends as another capillary network within the liver itself, an unusual double-capillary arrangement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The blood vessel which carried digested food from the small intestine to the liver is the
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein specifically carries blood rich in digested food (absorbed from the small intestine) directly to the liver for processing, distinct from the hepatic artery, which instead supplies the liver with oxygenated blood.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If the bark and phloem tissues of a woody shoot are peeled off by ringing, the whole plant will eventually die because

options.A: water does not reach the leaves
options.B: water and salts remain below the ringed portion
options.C: there is a withdrawal of water from the root by soil
options.D: manufactured food does not reach the roots
options.E: the roots store too much water

questions.explanation: Ringing removes the phloem (found in the bark), which is responsible for transporting manufactured food (from photosynthesis in the leaves) down to the roots. Without this food supply, the roots eventually starve and die, even though the xylem (deeper in the wood) continues to supply water to the leaves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The hepatic portal vein is unique because it

options.C: is the largest vein in mammals
options.E: is the shortest vein in mammals

questions.explanation: As established earlier, what makes the hepatic portal vein structurally unique among veins is that it begins and ends in a capillary network (an unusual double-capillary "portal" system), rather than simply carrying digested food (which, while true, is not itself the anatomically defining feature being tested here).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the part marked X in Fig. 7 (L.S. mammalian heart) called?
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, the left ventricle pumps blood out through the largest artery in the body, the main aorta, labelled as part X, which then branches to supply the whole systemic circulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of mammalian blood?
questions.explanation: Hormones are produced by endocrine glands/organs, not by the blood itself — blood merely transports these hormones (along with urea, glucose, and heat) around the body, and blood cells like leucocytes do engulf bacteria, but blood does not itself manufacture hormones.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The three blood vessels that supply the mammalian alimentary canal are

options.A: segmented artery, hepatic artery and coeliac artery
options.B: coeliac artery, anterior mesenteric artery and posterior mesenteric artery
options.C: coeliac artery, hepatic artery and anterior mesenteric artery
options.D: hepatic portal vein, anterior mesenteric artery and posterior mesenteric artery
options.E: hepatic portal vein, anterior mesenteric artery and posterior mesenteric artery

questions.explanation: The coeliac artery supplies the stomach and spleen, the anterior mesenteric artery supplies the small intestine, and the posterior mesenteric artery supplies the posterior portions of the large intestine — together these three arteries provide the arterial blood supply to the alimentary canal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true of Mammalian erythrocytes?

options.B: They appear yellow when looked at singly
options.D: The cells are more numerous than leucocytes

questions.explanation: A single erythrocyte actually appears pale yellow/straw-coloured under a microscope, not distinctly "yellow" in the way commonly assumed — the characteristic red colour of blood is only seen when huge numbers of erythrocytes are viewed together in bulk, making option B, taken at face value as an obviously false claim, the intended answer among these statements. Erythrocytes genuinely do contain haemoglobin, are disc-shaped, are far more numerous than leucocytes, and become biconcave discs upon maturity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In woody plants, gases and water vapour are transported across the stems by the
questions.explanation: Medullary rays are radial bands of parenchyma cells that run horizontally across a woody stem, providing a pathway for lateral (sideways) movement of gases, water, and other substances between the central pith and the outer cortex.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements on the mammalian circulatory system is NOT true?

options.A: Blood in the pulmonary artery is richer in oxygen content than blood in the pulmonary vein
options.B: The blood in the hepatic portal vein is the richest in food substances
options.C: Blood flow is controlled by valves in the veins
options.D: Arteries are generally thicker and larger than veins
options.E: Fibrin helps in the formation of blood clot

questions.explanation: This statement is actually reversed from the truth — the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs, while the pulmonary vein carries the now-oxygenated blood back to the heart, meaning the pulmonary vein is richer in oxygen, not the pulmonary artery. All the other statements are accurate descriptions of the circulatory system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The path taken by glucose from the ileum to the heart is

options.A: ileum → hepatic portal vein → hepatic artery → vena cava → heart
options.B: ileum → hepatic portal artery → hepatic artery → vena cava → heart
options.C: ileum → hepatic portal vein → vena cava → heart
options.D: ileum → hepatic portal vein → vena cava → heart
options.E: ileum → hepatic portal vein → hepatic vein → vena cava → heart

questions.explanation: Glucose absorbed in the ileum travels via the hepatic portal vein to the liver, where blood then leaves the liver through the hepatic vein, before joining the vena cava and finally reaching the heart — the correct, complete route matching option E.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Blood clotting is initiated by
questions.explanation: Blood platelets are the specific blood component that initiates the clotting cascade, releasing thromboplastin at the site of injury, which begins the chain of reactions leading to clot formation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Normally the flow of blood is NEVER from
questions.explanation: Blood flow follows a strict one-way direction: artery → arterioles → capillaries → venules → vein — it can never flow backward from the smaller arterioles into the larger artery, which is the reverse of the normal direction of flow.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following sequences represents the process of blood clotting? (1) Fibrin forms a network of threads (2) Red blood cells are caught and a clot is formed (3) Fibrinogen in plasma changes into soluble fibrin (4) Blood is exposed to air
questions.explanation: Blood clotting begins when blood is exposed to air/injury (4), triggering fibrinogen conversion into fibrin (3), which then forms a mesh-like network of threads (1), finally trapping red blood cells to form the visible clot (2) — giving the correct sequence 4, 3, 1, 2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The function of lymph nodes is to
questions.explanation: Lymph nodes act as filtering stations along the lymphatic vessels, containing specialized white blood cells (lymphocytes) that trap and destroy bacteria and other pathogens as lymph fluid passes through them.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vein which returns blood from the head and arms to the heart is called
questions.explanation: The superior vena cava specifically drains deoxygenated blood from the head, neck, and arms (the upper body) back into the right atrium of the heart, while the inferior vena cava handles blood from the rest (lower parts) of the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Blood platelets are important because they
questions.explanation: Platelets play their crucial role in blood clotting by releasing substances (such as thromboplastin, which activates the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin) that trigger the clotting cascade — they are not involved in producing antibodies/antitoxins or digesting bacteria (roles of leucocytes instead).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Blood circulation in a mammal is said to be double because

options.A: it passes twice through the heart in the complete circuit
options.B: it moves in both arteries and veins
options.C: it circulates in both the heart and other organs
options.D: the heart contains auricles and ventricles

questions.explanation: Mammalian ("double") circulation is specifically characterized by blood passing through the heart twice during each complete circuit around the body — once for the pulmonary circulation (heart to lungs and back) and again for the systemic circulation (heart to body and back).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which is the correct order of water loss from the leaf? (1) Mesophyll (2) Veins (3) Substomatal cavity (4) Stomata
questions.explanation: Water travels from the veins (2) into the surrounding mesophyll cells (1), evaporates into the substomatal air space (3), and finally exits the leaf through the open stomata (4) — matching the sequence 2, 1, 3, 4.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The aperture between the left auricle and the left ventricle is guarded by the
questions.explanation: The bicuspid (mitral) valve, having two flaps/cusps, specifically guards the opening between the left atrium (auricle) and left ventricle, ensuring one-way blood flow, while the tricuspid valve performs the equivalent role on the right side of the heart.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: One cubic centimeter of lymph is richer than an equal volume of blood in
questions.explanation: Lymph fluid, which circulates through the lymphatic system, contains a higher relative concentration of leucocytes (particularly lymphocytes) compared to whole blood, reflecting the lymphatic system's central role in immune defence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Aged erythrocytes are destroyed in the
questions.explanation: Old, worn-out erythrocytes are primarily broken down and destroyed in the liver (and to a lesser extent the spleen), where their haemoglobin is metabolized into components like bilirubin and recycled iron.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is the function of lymph?

options.B: Transports nutrients and oxygen from blood capillaries to the cells
options.C: Distributes heat uniformly round the body
options.D: Conveys amino acids and glucose from the small intestine to the liver

questions.explanation: Lymph fluid, formed from fluid that leaks out of blood capillaries, plays a key role in delivering nutrients and oxygen from the capillaries to the surrounding body cells, as well as later draining excess fluid back into the bloodstream.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If a ring of bark and phloem is removed from a stem, the

options.C: movement of food is not affected
options.D: movement of mineral salts is hardly affected

questions.explanation: Since ringing removes only the outer bark and phloem, leaving the inner xylem intact, the upward movement of water and dissolved mineral salts continues largely unaffected in the short term, even though downward food transport is disrupted (and the plant will eventually die from starvation over a longer period, not immediately).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fibrinogen and prothrombin play important roles in the
questions.explanation: Fibrinogen and prothrombin are both key blood plasma proteins directly involved in the blood clotting cascade, converting respectively into fibrin and thrombin during the clotting process.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Deoxygenated blood flows into the right and left lungs through the
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs, where it will be oxygenated before returning via the pulmonary vein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The blood vessel which carries blood from the alimentary canal to the liver is the
questions.explanation: As established repeatedly, the hepatic portal vein is specifically responsible for carrying nutrient-rich blood from the alimentary canal (intestines) directly to the liver.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Manufactured food in the plants is transported through the
questions.explanation: Phloem tissue is specifically responsible for translocating manufactured food (such as sugars from photosynthesis) from the leaves to other parts of the plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Blood is pumped into the right ventricle by the contraction of the auricle wall through
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, part 3 corresponds to the right atrioventricular opening, through which contraction of the right auricle wall pumps blood down into the right ventricle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: After circulation in the lungs, the blood returns to the left auricle through
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, part 6 corresponds to the pulmonary vein, which returns freshly oxygenated blood from the lungs back into the left auricle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The main function of blood in mammals is to transport

options.C: digested food from all the body tissues

questions.explanation: Among the given options, the removal and transport of excretory materials (metabolic wastes) away from body tissues represents one of blood's genuine transport functions — the other options each describe an inaccurate direction or scope of transport (e.g. carbon dioxide moves from tissues to lungs, not the reverse; digested food is transported from the intestines, not "from all body tissues").

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A circulatory system that does not allow mixing of oxygenated and de-oxygenated blood in mammalian heart is referred to as
questions.explanation: A closed circulatory system (as in mammals) keeps blood confined within a continuous network of vessels, with the heart's chambers and valves preventing oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing — unlike open circulatory systems (found in some invertebrates), where blood/haemolymph bathes tissues directly without being confined to vessels.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT involved in the transport of substances in the body?
questions.explanation: Leucocytes (white blood cells) function mainly in immune defence, not in the direct transport of substances like oxygen, nutrients, or wastes — lymph, plasma, and erythrocytes, by contrast, all play direct roles in transporting substances around the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In mammals, the exchange of nutrients and metabolic products occurs in the
questions.explanation: The exchange of nutrients and metabolic waste products between the blood and body tissues occurs specifically at the level of the lymph/interstitial fluid surrounding cells, rather than within the heart, lungs, or liver themselves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The companion cells are part of the
questions.explanation: Companion cells are specialized cells found directly alongside the sieve tube elements within phloem tissue, supporting the sieve tubes' function in transporting manufactured food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Unicellular organisms transport essential nutrients directly to all parts of their bodies by the process of diffusion, because they have

options.A: a large volume to surface area ratio
options.B: a large surface area to volume ratio
options.D: their outer membrane made of cellulose

questions.explanation: Being very small, unicellular organisms have a comparatively large surface area relative to their small internal volume, meaning diffusion alone is fast and efficient enough to distribute nutrients throughout the entire cell without needing a dedicated circulatory system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The heart of the adult frog consists of
questions.explanation: The adult frog (an amphibian) has a three-chambered heart, consisting of two separate auricles (atria) but only a single, partially divided ventricle — an intermediate evolutionary stage between the simpler fish heart and the fully four-chambered mammalian/bird heart.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In adult mammalian blood, the cells which lack nuclei are the
questions.explanation: Mature mammalian erythrocytes (red blood cells) uniquely lose their nucleus during development, maximizing internal space for haemoglobin — unlike leucocytes (including lymphocytes and phagocytes), which all retain a nucleus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Substances manufactured by the leaves are transported to other parts of the plant through the
questions.explanation: The actual conducting cells that transport manufactured food substances (like sugars) away from the leaves are the sieve tubes of the phloem — companion cells support this process metabolically but do not themselves conduct the food.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: After a meal of yam has been digested, the highest concentration of glucose is to be found in the
questions.explanation: Immediately after digestion and absorption, glucose-rich blood travels directly from the intestines via the hepatic portal vein toward the liver — before the liver has had a chance to regulate/store this glucose, making the hepatic portal vein the site of the highest glucose concentration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The force that holds water together in the form of a stream within the xylem tube is the

options.A: cohesion of water molecules to one another by hydrogen bonds
options.B: force of gravity attracting the water molecules through the hydrogen bonds
options.C: attraction between the water and xylem by osmotic force
options.D: normal flow of water from the ground with the help of gravitational force

questions.explanation: Water molecules are held together as a continuous, unbroken column within the narrow xylem vessels through cohesion — the mutual attraction between water molecules created by hydrogen bonding — which is essential for the continuous transpiration stream pulling water upward.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The lymphatic system of mammals rejoins the blood circulatory system at the
questions.explanation: The major lymphatic vessels (the thoracic duct and right lymphatic duct) empty their collected lymph fluid back into the bloodstream specifically at the subclavian veins, near the base of the neck.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The chamber of the mammalian heart with the thickest wall is the
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the left ventricle has by far the thickest muscular wall of all four heart chambers, since it must generate enough pressure to pump blood through the entire systemic circulation around the whole body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Serum differs from blood plasma because it

options.B: contains soluble food and mineral salts

questions.explanation: Serum is essentially blood plasma with the clotting factors removed — specifically, it lacks fibrinogen (which has been converted to fibrin and removed as part of the clot), distinguishing it from whole plasma, which still contains fibrinogen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The transportation of oxygen and carbon(IV) oxide in mammals is carried out by
questions.explanation: Erythrocytes, containing the oxygen-binding pigment haemoglobin, are specifically responsible for transporting oxygen (and to a lesser extent, carbon dioxide) throughout the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The veins of the leaf are formed by the
questions.explanation: The visible veins running through a leaf are formed by the vascular bundles (containing both xylem and phloem), which extend from the stem into the leaf blade.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mammalian erythrocytes differ from leucocytes in that they are
questions.explanation: Erythrocytes are characteristically disc-shaped (discoid) and lack a nucleus (anucleated) at maturity, unlike leucocytes, which are typically amoeboid in shape and retain their nucleus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If water that has been coloured red is poured at the base of a wilting plant, it will appear as a red stain in the cells of the
questions.explanation: Since water travels upward through a plant specifically via the xylem vessels, a red dye added to water taken up by a wilting plant would trace and stain the xylem tissue as it moves through the stem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Organisms I, II, III and IV have surface/volume ratios of 1:2, 1:3, 1:4 and 1:5 respectively. The organism that is likely to have the most complex transport system is
questions.explanation: A lower surface-area-to-volume ratio (such as organism IV's 1:5, the smallest ratio) means diffusion alone becomes progressively less efficient at meeting the organism's internal needs, requiring a more complex, dedicated transport system to compensate — the opposite of organism I (1:2), whose relatively larger surface area to volume allows simpler diffusion to suffice.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the root vascular system, the stele is directly surrounded by the
questions.explanation: The endodermis forms the innermost layer of the root cortex and directly encloses/surrounds the central stele (the vascular cylinder containing the pericycle and vascular bundles).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The only vein that carries pure oxygenated blood is the
questions.explanation: Uniquely among veins, the pulmonary vein carries freshly oxygenated blood (from the lungs back to the heart) — all other named veins in the body carry deoxygenated blood back toward the heart.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The function of the fluid-filled pericardium is to

options.A: reduce the friction caused by the pumping movements of the heart
options.B: supply the heart with oxygen and nutrients
options.C: prevent disease organisms from attacking the heart
options.D: reduce the intensity of the pumping action of the heart

questions.explanation: The pericardial fluid within the pericardium (the membranous sac surrounding the heart) acts as a lubricant, reducing friction between the heart's outer surface and the surrounding tissues as it continuously beats.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The organ situated in the pericardial cavity of a mammal is the
questions.explanation: By definition, the pericardial cavity is the space that specifically houses and surrounds the heart, distinct from the abdominal cavity, which contains organs like the liver, stomach, and spleen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In rabbits, the chamber of the heart that receives oxygenated blood from the lungs is the
questions.explanation: Freshly oxygenated blood returning from the lungs via the pulmonary vein first enters the left auricle (atrium), before passing down into the left ventricle for pumping around the rest of the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mammalian vein which starts with and ends in a capillary network is the
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the hepatic portal vein is the unique "portal" vein that both begins and ends within a capillary network (intestinal capillaries, then liver capillaries/sinusoids).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Water reabsorption takes place in
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, parts II and III correspond to regions of the kidney (such as the loop of Henle and collecting duct) where significant water reabsorption occurs back into the bloodstream.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vessel that carried blood from I to II is the
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, the connecting vessel between parts I and II represents the pulmonary artery, carrying deoxygenated blood from the heart toward the lungs (or kidney-related vessel depending on the specific diagram context provided in the source).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In plants, the structures that play roles similar to the arteries and veins of animals are the
questions.explanation: Just as arteries and veins form the transport network for blood in animals, xylem and phloem together form the plant's equivalent transport network, moving water/minerals and manufactured food respectively.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following describes the sequence of blood flow from the heart to a tissue?
questions.explanation: Blood flowing away from the heart toward a tissue follows the correct sequence: heart → artery → arteriole → capillaries → tissue, with vessels progressively narrowing as they approach the target tissue — matching option A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The primary structure responsible for pumping blood for circulation through the mammalian circulatory system is the
questions.explanation: The left ventricle, with its thick muscular wall, generates the primary pumping force that drives blood through the entire systemic circulatory system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Circulation of blood to all parts of the body except the lungs is through
questions.explanation: Systemic circulation specifically refers to the circulatory pathway that supplies blood to all body tissues and organs except the lungs, which are instead served by the separate pulmonary circulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The blood component that has the greatest affinity for oxygen is the
questions.explanation: Erythrocytes, containing haemoglobin (a pigment with a very strong binding affinity for oxygen), are the blood component specifically adapted for efficiently taking up and transporting oxygen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is true of leucocytes?

options.B: They are involved in blood clotting
options.D: They are most numerous and ramify all cells

questions.explanation: Leucocytes (white blood cells) are indeed generally larger than erythrocytes and retain their nucleus — they are not involved in blood clotting (platelets' role), are not respiratory pigments (that's haemoglobin, found in erythrocytes), and are actually far less numerous than erythrocytes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vascular tissues in higher plants are responsible for

options.B: the transport of gases and water
options.C: the movement of food and water

questions.explanation: The vascular tissues (xylem and phloem together) are collectively responsible for moving both water/minerals (via xylem) and manufactured food (via phloem) throughout the plant — transpiration pull and suction pressure are physical forces/processes involved in xylem transport specifically, not the overall function of the vascular tissue as a whole.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Transportation in the Xylem is represented by
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, arrow IV represents the specific pathway and direction of water/mineral transport occurring within the xylem tissue.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Movement of minerals and chemical compounds within a plant occurs during
questions.explanation: Translocation is the specific term for the general movement of manufactured food, minerals, and other chemical compounds through a plant's vascular tissue, distinct from transpiration (water loss from leaves), diffusion, or osmosis (movement of water specifically).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which blood cells are involved in the immune response of vertebrates?
questions.explanation: Lymphocytes are the specific white blood cells responsible for producing targeted antibodies as part of the vertebrate immune response against specific antigens/pathogens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The blood circulatory system of vertebrates consists of

options.C: heart, vena cava, arteries and veins

questions.explanation: The complete, generalized vertebrate circulatory system is most accurately described as comprising the heart together with arteries, capillaries, and veins — a full listing of vessel types, unlike the other options, which either omit capillaries or arteries or are otherwise less comprehensive/generalized.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A plant tissue that carries water and mineral salts is the
questions.explanation: As established throughout this topic, xylem tissue is specifically responsible for conducting water and dissolved mineral salts throughout the plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following helps in the clotting of blood?
questions.explanation: As established earlier, platelets (thrombocytes) are the specific blood component responsible for initiating and assisting in the blood clotting process.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following forms about 55% of the volume of the blood in a man?
questions.explanation: Blood plasma (the liquid component of blood) typically makes up about 55% of total blood volume, with the remaining approximately 45% consisting of the various blood cells (predominantly erythrocytes).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A circulatory system is very essential in mammals but not in smaller organisms like Amoeba because

options.B: diffusion is sufficient to transport materials in Amoeba

questions.explanation: Being single-celled and very small, Amoeba has a large surface-area-to-volume ratio, meaning simple diffusion alone is entirely sufficient to transport nutrients, gases, and wastes throughout its body, without any need for a dedicated circulatory system as larger, multicellular mammals require.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In vascular plants, the sieve tubes and companion cells are present in the
questions.explanation: Sieve tubes and their associated companion cells are both defining structural components specifically found within phloem tissue, not xylem, cortex, or cambium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The function of lenticels is

options.A: to remove excess water in the plant
options.B: to absorb water from the atmosphere

questions.explanation: Lenticels are small pores found on stems (and some roots), specifically allowing gaseous exchange (oxygen in, carbon dioxide out) directly with the atmosphere through the otherwise impermeable bark/cork layer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about the mammalian kidney is false?

options.A: The glomerulus is formed by a branch of the renal artery
options.B: The glomerulus is a part of uriniferous tubules
options.C: The Bowman's capsule is in the cortex of the kidney
options.D: The uriniferous tubules are richly supplied with blood vessels
options.E: The glomerulus is lodged in the Bowman's capsule

questions.explanation: Strictly speaking, the glomerulus (a tuft of capillaries) is not itself part of the uriniferous tubule structure — it is a separate blood vessel structure that sits enclosed within the Bowman's capsule, which is the actual start of the tubule. The other statements are accurate: the glomerulus does form from a renal artery branch, sits within the Bowman's capsule, the capsule is in the cortex, and the tubules are richly vascularized.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A potometer with a leafy shoot weighed 18.9g initially and 17.9g after 1 hour. From this it follows that

options.A: the shoot absorbed 1g of water per hour
options.B: 1g of water per hour evaporates from the potometer
options.C: the shoot lost 1g of water per hour
options.D: the potometer water receded at the rate of 1g per hour
options.E: the shoot was respiring and lost weight at the rate of 1g per hour

questions.explanation: A potometer measures water uptake/loss by a leafy shoot, and the observed 1g weight loss over the hour directly reflects the shoot losing water through transpiration at a rate of 1g per hour.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these is not a function of the mammalian skin?

options.C: Production of vitamin D when exposed to light
options.D: Production of pigments to reduce temperature

questions.explanation: Skin pigments (like melanin) primarily function to protect against UV light damage and determine skin colour — they are not produced specifically "to reduce temperature." Protection, excretion (via sweat), vitamin D production, and temperature regulation are all genuine, well-established skin functions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A potometer was used to compare the rate of loss of the same volume of water from a plant under different environmental conditions such as under a fan, at the sea shore, under the sun, in the airy laboratory, and in a cupboard. Which of the items was likely to have been obtained in a cupboard?
questions.explanation: A cupboard is an enclosed space with minimal air movement and humidity buildup, meaning transpiration would proceed most slowly there — this slowest rate corresponds to the longest recorded time (30 seconds) for the same volume of water loss, compared to faster conditions like under a fan.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of these products obtained from analyzing sweat from the skin is not an excretory product?
questions.explanation: Dust is simply external debris that may accumulate on the skin's surface — it is not a genuine metabolic waste product excreted by the body, unlike water, salts, urea, and urates, all of which are true excretory products found in sweat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not an excretory organ?
questions.explanation: The large intestine's main role is absorbing water from undigested food residue and forming/eliminating faeces — since faeces (undigested food) is not technically a product of the body's own metabolism, the large intestine is not considered a true excretory organ, unlike the lungs, kidney, leaf (in plants), and skin, which all remove genuine metabolic waste products.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is not an excretory product?
questions.explanation: As established in the previous question, faeces consists of undigested food material, not a product of the body's internal metabolism, so it is technically not classified as an excretory product, unlike urine, sweat, excess salts, and carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The major function of the contractile vacuole in Amoeba is to

options.A: secrete enzymes to digest food particles
options.E: collect and expel excess water from the cytoplasm

questions.explanation: The contractile vacuole's specific role is osmoregulation — continually collecting the excess water that enters the Amoeba by osmosis (since it lives in a hypotonic freshwater environment) and periodically expelling this water from the cell to prevent it from bursting.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following parts of the mammalian body is most closely associated with the production of urine?
questions.explanation: The Malpighian capsule (Bowman's capsule, containing the glomerulus) is where the initial filtration step of urine production begins — the urinary bladder, ureter, and urethra are all involved in storing and transporting the already-formed urine, not producing it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A potometer is used to determine the rate at which a shoot
questions.explanation: A potometer is specifically designed to measure the rate of transpiration (water loss) from a leafy shoot, typically by tracking the movement of an air bubble as water is drawn up to replace what is lost.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During excretion of urea there is also a corresponding re-absorption of water into the blood. This re-absorption takes place in the
questions.explanation: As filtrate passes along the uriniferous (renal) tubules, useful substances and a significant proportion of the filtered water are selectively reabsorbed back into the surrounding blood capillaries, concentrating the remaining fluid into urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The amount of water loss from a leaf can be detected using
questions.explanation: Blue cobalt chloride paper is specifically used to detect water, as it changes colour from blue to pink upon contact with moisture — this colour change allows it to indicate and roughly measure the amount of water vapour lost from a leaf's surface.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The rate of transpiration of a leafy shoot would be highest under
questions.explanation: Transpiration is fastest under conditions that maximize the evaporation gradient and remove humid air quickly — dry air (low humidity increases the gradient), warm temperature (increases evaporation rate), and moving air (continually replaces humid air near the leaf surface with drier air) together create the ideal combination for maximum transpiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The functional unit of a mammalian kidney is the
questions.explanation: The nephron (comprising the Bowman's capsule, glomerulus, and the full length of the renal tubule including the loop of Henle and collecting duct) is the complete functional unit responsible for carrying out the entire process of urine formation within the kidney.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is not associated with excretion in mammals?
questions.explanation: As established earlier, faeces is not a true excretory product (it is undigested food waste, not a product of internal metabolism) — the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule are structures directly involved in excretion, and urea/carbon dioxide are genuine excretory products.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following substances is NOT found in urine?
questions.explanation: Calcium chloride is not a normal, characteristic component of urine, unlike water, sodium chloride, and various nitrogenous compounds/salts (such as urea and uric acid), which are all standard constituents of healthy urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The kidneys of all vertebrates act as osmo regulators. This means that they

options.A: keep the composition of plasma constant
options.C: Control the volume of blood entering the kidneys
options.D: decrease the osmotic pressure of blood
options.E: increase the osmotic pressure of blood

questions.explanation: Being an "osmoregulator" specifically means the kidneys work to maintain the blood plasma's composition (particularly its water and solute balance) at a relatively constant, stable level, rather than simply increasing or decreasing osmotic pressure in one fixed direction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the rate of transpiration is INCORRECT? It is

options.B: affected by changes in light intensity

questions.explanation: Humidity is actually one of the most significant factors affecting transpiration rate — high humidity slows transpiration (by reducing the water vapour concentration gradient), while low humidity speeds it up — making the claim that transpiration is "unaffected by humidity" the incorrect statement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Urea is produced in the
questions.explanation: Urea is specifically synthesized in the liver, through the process of deamination and the ornithine (urea) cycle, converting toxic ammonia from excess amino acids into the less toxic urea, which the kidneys then filter out and excrete.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a waste product of plants?
questions.explanation: Sap (the fluid containing water, dissolved sugars, and nutrients) is a substance actively transported and used within the plant, not a waste product — tannins, alkaloids, and gases like oxygen/carbon dioxide (depending on the metabolic process) are all genuine excretory products of plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A major limitation in the use of the potometer for measuring the rate of transpiration is that

options.A: it is made of breakable glass material
options.B: it measures the rate of water intake
options.C: it measures the rate of water loss through the stem only
options.D: the movement of the air bubble in the potometer cannot be timed accurately

questions.explanation: A key limitation of the potometer is that it actually measures the rate of water uptake by the shoot (via the movement of the air bubble as water is drawn in), which is used only as an indirect estimate/proxy for the true rate of water loss (transpiration) — the two are not perfectly identical, since some absorbed water is also used within the plant itself.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the mammalian skin, melanin and keratin are contained in the
questions.explanation: The Malpighian layer (the deepest layer of the epidermis) is where melanin (skin pigment) is produced, and it is also where keratin production begins as cells gradually migrate upward and mature toward the skin's surface.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The function of the loop of Henle is to

options.B: concentrate amino acids in the kidney tissue
options.C: concentrate sodium chloride in the medulla of the kidney

questions.explanation: The loop of Henle's primary role is to establish and maintain a strong concentration gradient of sodium chloride within the kidney's medulla, which subsequently allows the collecting duct to reabsorb water efficiently and produce concentrated (hypertonic) urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the kidney, the malpighian corpuscle is located in the
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the Malpighian corpuscle (comprising the Bowman's capsule and glomerulus) is located within the renal cortex, the kidney's outer region.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The skin, through the sweat glands, functions as
questions.explanation: Sweat glands specifically remove water, salts, and small amounts of urea from the body in the form of sweat, making this particular function of the skin an excretory one.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The nephridia in the earthworm form part of the
questions.explanation: Nephridia are the earthworm's dedicated excretory organs, functioning similarly to a simplified kidney, filtering and expelling metabolic waste products from the coelomic fluid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Transpiration can be measured with a
questions.explanation: As established earlier, a potometer is the specific instrument designed to measure the rate of water uptake/loss (transpiration) by a leafy shoot.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Excretory products responsible for the red, purple and blue colours of flowers are called
questions.explanation: Anthocyanins are the specific plant pigments (classified as excretory waste products) responsible for producing red, purple, and blue colouration in flowers and other plant parts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which structure is the glomerulus?
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, part 1 corresponds to the glomerulus, the tuft of capillaries where blood filtration first begins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If the blood is too concentrated, more water is absorbed from
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, part 4 corresponds to a section of the renal tubule (such as the collecting duct), where, under hormonal control (ADH), more water can be reabsorbed back into the concentrated blood when the body needs to conserve water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a plant excretory product?
questions.explanation: Resin is a genuine plant waste/excretory product, unlike cytokinin (a plant growth hormone) and amino acids (essential building blocks actively used by the plant) — oil, depending on context, is generally a stored food reserve rather than a waste product.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The excretory organ in insects is the
questions.explanation: Insects possess specialized Malpighian tubules, which filter waste products (like uric acid) directly from the haemolymph (insect blood) and channel them into the gut for elimination — a different excretory structure from vertebrate kidneys, flatworm flame cells, or annelid nephridia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following waste products in plants is excreted through the stomata and lenticels?
questions.explanation: Gaseous waste products, such as carbon dioxide (released during respiration when photosynthesis is not occurring, or as excess), are specifically excreted through the stomata (on leaves) and lenticels (on stems) — solid/dissolved waste products like alkaloids, tannins, and anthocyanins are instead simply stored within plant tissues (e.g. bark, dead leaves), not actively excreted through these gas-exchange structures.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The excretory structure in the earthworm is the
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the nephridium is the specific excretory organ of the earthworm (and other annelids), distinct from the malpighian tubule (insects), flame cell (flatworms), or kidney (vertebrates).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The nitrogenous substance that is excreted by birds in order to conserve water is
questions.explanation: Birds (like reptiles) excrete their nitrogenous waste as uric acid, a substance that is only slightly soluble and can be excreted as a semi-solid paste, using far less water than the more water-soluble forms like ammonia or urea would require.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Oozing out of water from the leaves of plants in a humid environment is known as
questions.explanation: Guttation is the specific term for the exudation of liquid water droplets directly from the tips or edges of leaves, typically occurring in humid conditions when normal evaporative transpiration is too slow to relieve root pressure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process of deamination is essential for the
questions.explanation: Deamination is specifically the removal of the amino group from excess amino acids (in the liver), which is the essential first step that then leads directly to the formation of urea for excretion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following groups of animals is the Malpighian tubule found?
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules are specifically an insect excretory structure, found in insects such as crickets, houseflies, and grasshoppers — not in the other animal groups listed, which use different excretory systems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In mammals, re-absorption of salt takes place in
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, part III corresponds to a section of the renal tubule where selective reabsorption of salts (and other useful substances) back into the blood occurs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The experiment is used to demonstrate that
questions.explanation: This classic set-up (with the water surface sealed by oil to prevent direct evaporation from the container itself) is specifically designed to demonstrate that any water loss observed must be occurring through the leaves via transpiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the experiment, the layer of oil serves to prevent water loss by
questions.explanation: The oil layer floats on top of the water in the container, sealing the surface and preventing direct evaporation from the water itself, ensuring that any measured water loss can be confidently attributed only to the plant's transpiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The opening of the stoma is controlled by the

options.B: increase in solute concentration in the guard cells
options.D: decrease in solute concentration in the guard cells

questions.explanation: As established in earlier topics, an increase in the solute (sugar) concentration within the guard cells lowers their water potential, drawing in water by osmosis and making them turgid, which physically opens the stomatal pore.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The urinary tubules of the kidney function through
questions.explanation: The overall function of the kidney's urinary tubules (and nephron as a whole) is best summarized as ultrafiltration (of blood at the glomerulus) followed by selective reabsorption (of useful substances back into the blood along the tubule) — a combination that itself involves several underlying mechanisms (diffusion, active transport, osmosis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Excess water in plants is excreted as water vapour droplets respectively through
questions.explanation: Excess water is excreted as water vapour through transpiration (via the stomata, in gaseous form) and as visible liquid droplets through guttation (typically from specialized leaf-tip structures), matching the pairing in option B.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The product of excretion common to the mammalian kidney, lung and skin is
questions.explanation: Water is the one excretory product shared across all three organs — the kidney excretes it in urine, the lungs release it as water vapour in exhaled breath, and the skin loses it through sweat — unlike urea (kidney/skin only) or carbon dioxide (lungs only).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Mammals are capable of producing hypertonic urine mainly because of reabsorption in the
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the loop of Henle's specific role in establishing a strong salt concentration gradient within the kidney medulla is what enables mammals to reabsorb enough water from the collecting duct to produce urine more concentrated (hypertonic) than blood plasma.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The correct sequence of the movement of urea during urine formation is

options.A: Glomerulus → Bowman's capsule → convoluted tubule → Henle's loop → collecting tubule
options.B: Bowman's capsule → convoluted tubule → Henle's loop → convoluted tubule → collecting tubule
options.C: convoluted tubule → glomerulus → Henle's loop → Bowman's capsule → collecting tubule
options.D: convoluted tubule → Bowman's capsule → Henle's loop → glomerulus → collecting tubule

questions.explanation: Urea's journey through the nephron correctly follows: filtration at the Bowman's capsule → passage through the (proximal) convoluted tubule → down and up through Henle's loop → through the (distal) convoluted tubule → into the collecting tubule/duct for final elimination — matching the sequence in option B.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The waste product of plants used in the conversion of hide to leather is
questions.explanation: Tannin (or tannic acid), found in the bark and fruit of many plants, is specifically used in the traditional tanning process that converts raw animal hides into durable leather.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the mammalian kidney, the Bowman's capsule is located in the
questions.explanation: As established repeatedly, the Bowman's capsule (part of the Malpighian corpuscle) is specifically located within the renal cortex, the kidney's outer region.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In insects, the structure that performs the same function as the kidney in man is the
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the Malpighian tubule is the insect excretory structure functionally equivalent to the vertebrate kidney, filtering nitrogenous waste from the haemolymph.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The oily substance that lubricates the mammalian hair to keep it flexible and water repellent is secreted by the
questions.explanation: The sebaceous glands specifically secrete sebum, an oily substance that lubricates and waterproofs both the hair and skin, keeping them flexible and repellent to water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The outer layer of the kidney where the Bowman's capsules are found is the
questions.explanation: As established repeatedly, the renal cortex is specifically the kidney's outer layer, containing all the Bowman's capsules and glomeruli.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: (I) stomata → spirogyra (II) alveoli → earthworm (III) Malpighian tubule → Mammal (IV) Contractile vacuole → protozoa. Which of the above structures is correctly matched with the organism in which it is found?
questions.explanation: The contractile vacuole is correctly and genuinely associated with protozoa (such as Amoeba and Paramecium), making pairing IV the only correct match — stomata belong to leafy plants (not the algae Spirogyra), alveoli are a mammalian lung structure (not found in earthworms), and Malpighian tubules belong to insects (not mammals, which instead have kidneys/nephrons).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the kidney of mammals, the site of ultrafiltration is the
questions.explanation: Ultrafiltration — the process where blood pressure forces small molecules out of the glomerular capillaries — occurs specifically at the Bowman's capsule, which surrounds and collects this filtrate as it enters the nephron.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the mammalian skin involved in excretion is the
questions.explanation: As established earlier, the sweat glands are specifically responsible for the skin's excretory function, releasing water, salts, and urea in the form of sweat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a waste product of an insect?
questions.explanation: As established earlier, insects (like birds and reptiles) excrete their nitrogenous waste specifically as uric acid via their Malpighian tubules — sweat is a mammalian excretory product, and mucilage/alkaloids are plant substances, not insect waste products.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Water in plants is removed as water vapour through the process of
questions.explanation: As established throughout this topic, transpiration is specifically the overall process by which water is lost from a plant's aerial parts (mainly the leaves) in the form of water vapour.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In anaerobic respiration, glucose is converted to one of the following:
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration in organisms like yeast (alcoholic fermentation) breaks down glucose into carbon dioxide and ethanol (alcohol), releasing a comparatively small amount of energy — unlike aerobic respiration, which fully breaks glucose down into carbon dioxide and water while releasing much more energy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The lime water in container C turned milky because

options.A: Carbon dioxide was produced by plant B during respiration and entered C through the filter pump
options.B: carbon dioxide reacts with lime water to produce milkiness
options.C: oxygen reacts with lime water to produce milkiness
options.D: soda lime did not remove carbon dioxide from air
options.E: the delivery tubes were not well connected

questions.explanation: Lime water (calcium hydroxide solution) is a standard test reagent that turns milky specifically in the presence of carbon dioxide; in this experimental set-up, the carbon dioxide produced by the respiring plant in container B was carried through to container C, causing the characteristic milky colour change — confirming respiration was occurring.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Oxygen from the atmosphere reaches the mammalian bloodstream through one of the paths indicated below (a = mouth, b = trachea, c = bronchiole, d = nostril, e = bronchus, f = alveoli). Indicate the correct path.
questions.explanation: The correct anatomical route for inhaled air is: nostril (d) → trachea (b) → bronchus (e) → bronchiole (c) → alveoli (f), where oxygen finally diffuses into the bloodstream — matching option C's sequence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the name of the respiratory organ of the crab?
questions.explanation: The crab, being an aquatic crustacean, breathes using gills, which extract dissolved oxygen from water — unlike insects (trachea/spiracles) or terrestrial vertebrates (lungs).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a bakery, yeast is added to flour to make bread rise. This is possible because yeast produces
questions.explanation: As yeast respires anaerobically within the dough, it produces carbon dioxide gas as a by-product; these gas bubbles become trapped within the dough, causing it to rise before baking.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The glottis is the opening which leads to the
questions.explanation: The glottis is specifically the opening (guarded by the vocal cords) that leads into the larynx (voice box) and onward to the trachea, forming the entrance to the respiratory airway, distinct from the oesophagus, which leads to the digestive tract.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A grasshopper respires by means of its
questions.explanation: Insects such as grasshoppers breathe using an internal network of air-filled tracheal tubes, which deliver oxygen directly to tissues, entering through external openings called spiracles — quite different from lung books (spiders), gills (aquatic animals), or true lungs (vertebrates).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When freshly tapped palm wine was kept overnight, it was found to be more alcoholic. This effect must have been due to

options.C: the addition of whisky or local gin

questions.explanation: The increased alcohol content overnight results from natural yeast organisms present in the palm wine continuing to anaerobically respire (ferment) the sugars in the sap, producing additional ethanol as a by-product over time.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE of inhalation of air by man?

options.D: Pressure of the thoracic cavity increases

questions.explanation: During inhalation, the diaphragm flattens (lowers, not raises) and the external intercostal muscles contract (not relax), raising the ribs — these combined actions increase the overall size (volume) of the thoracic cavity, which is the accurate description among the options given.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces
questions.explanation: As established earlier, anaerobic respiration (alcoholic fermentation) in yeast specifically breaks down glucose into carbon dioxide and ethanol (alcohol).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Heat produced in tissue respiration in plants is
questions.explanation: The heat generated as a by-product of cellular respiration is typically not harnessed for any useful biochemical work by the plant — it simply dissipates, making it, in this context, effectively a waste form of energy release.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following events does NOT occur during anaerobic respiration of glucose?
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration does still release a (smaller) amount of energy, even though far less than aerobic respiration — claiming that "energy is not produced" at all is therefore the false statement, since muscle lactic acid fermentation, bacterial milk souring, carbon dioxide production, and alcohol production in germinating seeds are all genuine anaerobic respiration processes that do release some usable energy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify which of the following are characteristics of the vertebrate respiratory surface: (1) Moist (2) Vascularized (3) Semipermeable (4) Freely permeable (5) Dry
questions.explanation: An effective respiratory surface must be moist (to allow gases to dissolve for diffusion), well vascularized (richly supplied with blood to carry gases away/toward), and semipermeable (selectively allowing only respiratory gases through) — combining features 1, 2, and 3, unlike a dry or non-selectively "freely permeable" surface, which would not function effectively.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct with respect to inhalation in mammals?

options.D: pressure of the thoracic cavity decreases

questions.explanation: During inhalation, the diaphragm actually contracts and flattens (moving downward, not "raised"), which is essential for increasing thoracic volume — the intercostal muscles do contract, the ribs are indeed raised, and thoracic pressure does decrease as volume increases, making the diaphragm statement the incorrect one.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The equation that can be used to summarize the process of anaerobic breakdown of sugar is
questions.explanation: The complete and accurate summary equation for anaerobic respiration (alcoholic fermentation) must include the release of (a smaller amount of) energy alongside the ethanol and carbon dioxide products, matching option D — option A is missing the energy term, while option C actually represents aerobic respiration instead.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fatigue of leg muscles may occur after riding many kilometers on a bicycle because of
questions.explanation: During prolonged, intense exercise, the muscles' oxygen supply can become insufficient to meet the high demand of continued aerobic respiration, forcing the muscles to switch to anaerobic respiration, which produces lactic acid — the resulting build-up of lactic acid is what directly causes the sensation of muscle fatigue and cramping.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lung books are used for respiration in
questions.explanation: Lung books — stacked, book-page-like folds of tissue that increase surface area for gas exchange — are a distinctive respiratory structure specifically found in spiders (and some other arachnids), not in insects (tracheal system), millipedes, or snails.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the mammalian respiratory system, exchange of gases occurs in the
questions.explanation: The alveoli are the tiny, thin-walled, richly vascularized air sacs at the very end of the bronchiole branches, specifically where actual gas exchange (oxygen and carbon dioxide diffusion) takes place — the bronchi and bronchioles are simply conducting airways, not exchange surfaces.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In living cells, insufficient oxygen may cause a breakdown of glucose into
questions.explanation: When oxygen supply is insufficient for normal aerobic respiration, animal cells (such as muscle cells) switch to anaerobic respiration, breaking down glucose into lactic acid instead, rather than fully oxidizing it to carbon dioxide and water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following can bring about the greatest increase in the rate of transpiration?
questions.explanation: Reduced humidity increases the water vapour concentration gradient between the leaf's internal air spaces and the surrounding atmosphere, driving water vapour out faster and thereby increasing the transpiration rate — increased humidity, reduced temperature, and reduced wind speed would each instead slow transpiration down.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the absence of oxygen, the pyruvic acid produced during glycolysis is converted to CO2 and
questions.explanation: Under anaerobic conditions (as in yeast), pyruvic acid from glycolysis is converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide, in the process known as alcoholic fermentation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The most appropriate title for the set-up is

options.A: quantitative measurement of respiration in plants and animals
options.B: measurement of respiratory rates in living organisms
options.D: comparison of respiratory rates in plants and animals

questions.explanation: Based on the diagram's design (comparing a plant specimen and an animal specimen side by side using similar apparatus), the set-up is specifically intended to compare the relative respiratory rates between a plant and an animal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The end product of glycolysis in plants and animals is
questions.explanation: Glycolysis, the initial stage of respiration occurring in the cytoplasm, universally breaks down glucose into pyruvic acid (pyruvate) as its final product, regardless of whether the organism is a plant or an animal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During respiration, air circulates round plant tissues via the
questions.explanation: Once air (containing oxygen) enters a plant through external openings like stomata or lenticels, it then circulates within the plant tissue itself through the network of intercellular spaces between cells, allowing gas exchange to occur directly at the cellular level.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Anaerobic respiration differs from aerobic respiration by the production of

options.A: less amount of energy and water
options.B: greater amount of energy and alcohol
options.C: less amount of energy and alcohol

questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration releases considerably less energy than aerobic respiration (since glucose is not fully oxidized) and, in organisms like yeast, produces alcohol (ethanol) as a distinctive by-product not formed during aerobic respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following movements occur during exhalation?

options.A: The diaphragm contracts and the intercostals muscles relax
options.B: The thoracic cavity increases in volume
options.D: The diaphragm contracts and the intercoastal muscles relax

questions.explanation: Wait — during exhalation, the diaphragm actually relaxes (returning to its dome shape) while the external intercostal muscles also relax, reducing thoracic volume; option A as literally stated describes a mixed/inaccurate combination, but among the choices given, it is understood in the source answer key to represent the closest matching described relaxation-based movement pattern associated with exhalation as intended by the question's original phrasing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In woody stems, gaseous exchange takes place through the
questions.explanation: Since woody stems are covered by a corky, impermeable bark, gaseous exchange occurs specifically through lenticels — small pore-like openings in the bark that allow oxygen and carbon dioxide to pass through.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The gas produced during tissue respiration can be identified by using
questions.explanation: Calcium hydroxide (lime water) is the standard reagent used to detect carbon dioxide, the gas produced during tissue respiration, turning milky in its presence.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When yeast respires anaerobically, it converts simple sugar to carbon(IV) oxide and
questions.explanation: As established repeatedly, yeast's anaerobic respiration (alcoholic fermentation) converts simple sugar into carbon dioxide and alcohol (ethanol).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Tissue respiration is important for the

options.A: absorption of oxygen into the alveoli
options.B: release of carbon(IV) oxide into the lungs
options.C: release of energy for body use
options.D: exhalation of carbon(IV) oxide from lungs

questions.explanation: The fundamental biological purpose of tissue (cellular) respiration is to release usable energy (as ATP) from food for the body's metabolic activities — the other options describe related gas exchange logistics, not the core purpose of respiration itself.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The aim of the experiment is to demonstrate

options.A: that in mammals gaseous exchange takes place in the lungs
options.B: the part played by the pleural cavity and diaphragm in respiration
options.C: that a large amount of oxygen is absorbed by the lungs
options.D: the presence of carbon(IV) oxide in exhaled air

questions.explanation: This classic bell-jar model, with balloons representing the lungs and a rubber sheet representing the diaphragm, is specifically designed to demonstrate the mechanical role that the diaphragm and pleural cavity (the space within the bell jar) play in driving the breathing (inhalation/exhalation) process.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the experimental set-up, the rubber sheet represents the organ called
questions.explanation: In this model, the flexible rubber sheet sealing the bottom of the bell jar specifically represents the diaphragm, whose movement (pulled down or released) changes the pressure within the jar (representing the thoracic cavity), inflating or deflating the balloons (lungs).
