Gasoline/petrol boils over a higher range ($70\ ^\circ\text{C} - 200\ ^\circ\text{C}$), kerosene boils around $175\ ^\circ\text{C} - 250\ ^\circ\text{C}$, and gas oil boils above $250\ ^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The industrial process for converting ammonia to trioxonitrate(V) acid is the
questions.explanation: The Ostwald process oxidizes ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) over a platinum-rhodium catalyst at high temperature to form nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$), which is further oxidized to $\text{NO}_2$ and absorbed in water to yield trioxonitrate(V) acid ($\text{HNO}_3$). The Haber process produces ammonia, and the Contact process produces sulphuric acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The densities of two gases A and B are $0.25\ \text{g dm}^{-3}$ and $1.0\ \text{g dm}^{-3}$ respectively. What is the rate of diffusion of A relative to B?
questions.explanation: By Graham's Law of Diffusion, $R_A / R_B = \sqrt{d_B / d_A} = \sqrt{1.0 / 0.25} = \sqrt{4} = 2$. Thus, gas A diffuses twice as fast as gas B, giving a ratio of 2:1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following parameters decreases as steam condenses to water?
questions.explanation: Steam (gas) has higher molecular disorder than liquid water. Condensation organizes the molecules into a more structured liquid phase, leading to a decrease in the entropy ($\Delta S < 0$) of the system.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If the free energy change ($\Delta G$) of a reaction is $-899\ \text{J mol}^{-1}$ and the entropy change ($\Delta S$) is $+10\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ at $25\ ^\circ\text{C}$, calculate the enthalpy change ($\Delta H$).
questions.explanation: Temperature $T = 25 + 273.15 = 298.15\ \text{K}$. Using $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The most suitable indicator for the titration between $\text{NaOH}(aq)$ and $\text{HCOOH}(aq)$ is
questions.explanation: The titration of a weak acid ($\text{HCOOH}$) with a strong base ($\text{NaOH}$) produces a basic salt ($\text{HCOONa}$) at equivalence, yielding a $\text{pH} > 7$ (around 8–9). Phenolphthalein, which changes colour in the $\text{pH}$ range $8.3 - 10.0$, is the correct indicator.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Millikan's main contribution to atomic theory was the determination of the
questions.explanation: Robert Millikan performed the famous oil-drop experiment in 1909, which measured the elementary electric charge of an electron ($e = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\ \text{C}$). J.J. Thomson determined the charge-to-mass ratio.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorine gas reacts directly with heated metals to form their respective higher chlorides except in which of the following reactions?
questions.explanation: Chlorine is a strong oxidizing agent and oxidizes iron directly to iron(III) chloride ($\text{FeCl}_3$), not iron(II) chloride ($\text{FeCl}_2$). The correct reaction is $3\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{Fe} \rightarrow 2\text{FeCl}_3$. Reaction A is incorrect as written.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Which of the following compounds exhibit hydrogen bonding between their molecules?
I. $\text{NH}_3$
II. $\text{HF}$
III. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$
IV. $\text{CH}_4$
questions.explanation: Intermolecular hydrogen bonding occurs when hydrogen is directly attached to small, highly electronegative atoms ($\text{N}$, $\text{O}$, $\text{F}$). Therefore, $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{HF}$, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ form hydrogen bonds. $\text{CH}_4$ contains non-polar $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bonds and lacks hydrogen bonding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Cancerous growths are treated by exposure to
questions.explanation: Gamma rays ($\gamma$-rays) are high-energy electromagnetic radiations with deep penetrating power. They are directed at targeted cancerous tissues in radiotherapy to destroy malignant cells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Potassium vapour burns in a non-luminous Bunsen flame with a
questions.explanation: Flame tests produce characteristic emission colours for alkali metals. Potassium gives a lilac/violet flame, sodium gives golden-yellow, and calcium gives brick-red.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following elements undergoes a net mass increase when heated strongly in open air?
questions.explanation: When magnesium is heated in air, it reacts with oxygen to form solid magnesium oxide: $2\text{Mg}(s) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{MgO}(s)$. The mass of the solid product ($\text{MgO}$) is greater than the original mass of magnesium metal due to the added mass of oxygen. Carbon, sulphur, and ethanol produce gaseous products ($\text{CO}_2$, $\text{SO}_2$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$) that escape into the atmosphere.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An oxide of formula $\text{XO}_2$ has a vapour density of 32. What is the atomic mass of element X?
questions.explanation: Relative molecular mass $= 2 \times \text{vapour density} = 2 \times 32 = 64\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$. For $\text{XO}_2$: $X + 2(16) = 64 \implies X + 32 = 64 \implies X = 32$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When ethene gas mixed with oxygen is passed over a silver catalyst at about $250\ ^\circ\text{C}$, the main product is
questions.explanation: The catalytic oxidation of ethene with air/oxygen over a silver catalyst at $250\ ^\circ\text{C} - 300\ ^\circ\text{C}$ yields epoxyethane (ethylene oxide): $2\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 + \text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ag}} 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many unpaired electrons are present in the cation $\text{X}^+$ where the atomic number of X is 16?
questions.explanation: Neutral atom $X$ ($Z = 16$, Sulphur) has ground-state electronic configuration $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^4$. Removing one electron to form $\text{X}^+$ gives the configuration $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^3$. According to Hund's rule, the 3 sub-shell electrons in $3p^3$ occupy separate $p$-orbitals with parallel spins ($3p_x^1 3p_y^1 3p_z^1$), giving 3 unpaired electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Magnesium ($\text{Mg}$) has a smaller atomic radius than Calcium ($\text{Ca}$) because

options.A: nuclear charge decreases across the period
options.B: valence electrons in Mg occupy a higher principal energy level
options.C: Mg has fewer electron shells than Ca
options.D: metallic bonding is weaker in Ca

questions.explanation: Magnesium ($Z = 12$) has 3 occupied energy shells ($2, 8, 2$), whereas calcium ($Z = 20$) has 4 occupied energy shells ($2, 8, 8, 2$). Atomic radius increases down a group due to the addition of principal electron shells. Thus, $\text{Mg}$ is smaller than $\text{Ca}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the laboratory preparation of ethyne from calcium dicarbide, the gas is passed through aqueous $\text{CuSO}_4$ solution to remove
questions.explanation: Crude ethyne generated from calcium dicarbide ($\text{CaC}_2$) contains impurities such as phosphine ($\text{PH}_3$) and hydrogen sulphide ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$). Passing the gas through acidified copper(II) sulphate or acidified potassium dichromate solution absorbs these impurities.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following compounds is commonly used as a mild antiseptic in eyewashes and minor burns?
questions.explanation: Boric acid ($\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3$) is a weak, non-irritating acid with mild antiseptic and antifungal properties, widely used in dilute aqueous solutions as an eye lotion and mild skin antiseptic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If $10.8\ \text{g}$ of silver is deposited in a silver coulometer connected in series with an acidulated water coulometer, what volume of oxygen gas (measured at s.t.p.) is liberated at the anode? [$\text{Ag} = 108$; $\text{Molar gas volume at s.t.p.} = 22.4\ \text{dm}^3\ \text{mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanation: Moles of $\text{Ag}$ deposited $= 10.8 / 108 = 0.10\ \text{mol}$. Cathode half-reaction: $\text{Ag}^+ + e^- \rightarrow \text{Ag}$. Thus, $0.10\ \text{mol}$ of electrons (or $0.10\ \text{F}$) passed through the circuit. Anode half-reaction for water electrolysis: $2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{O}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 4e^-$. $4\ \text{moles}$ of electrons liberate $1\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{O}_2$. Moles of $\text{O}_2 = 0.10 / 4 = 0.025\ \text{mol}$. Volume at s.t.p. $= 0.025 \times 22.4 = 0.56\ \text{dm}^3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A sample of $6.02\ \text{g}$ of hydrated washing soda, $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\cdot y\text{H}_2\text{O}$, was dissolved in water to make $500\ \text{cm}^3$ of solution. A $25\ \text{cm}^3$ portion of this solution required $32.10\ \text{cm}^3$ of $0.097\ \text{mol dm}^{-3}\ \text{HCl}$ for complete neutralization. Find the value of $y$. [$\text{Na} = 23, \text{H} = 1, \text{C} = 12, \text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanation: Equation: $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following carbohydrate polymers consists entirely of unbranched, straight chains of $\beta$-1,4-glycosidic linkages?
questions.explanation: Cellulose is a linear polymer of D-glucose units connected by $\beta$-1,4-glycosidic bonds, forming unbranched chains. Starch (amylopectin) and glycogen contain branched $\alpha$-1,6 linkages.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Paper chromatography separates mixtures based primarily on differences in

options.C: relative solubility between stationary and mobile phases

questions.explanation: Paper chromatography relies on partition and adsorption phenomena. Components of a mixture separate according to their relative solubilities in the mobile phase (solvent) compared to their affinity for the stationary phase (water bound in paper fibers).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An advantage of ordinary soaps over synthetic detergents is that soaps

options.B: are biodegradable and do not cause persistent water pollution
options.C: act effectively in strongly acidic solutions

questions.explanation: Soap molecules are sodium or potassium salts of natural fatty acids, which soil bacteria easily decompose (biodegradable). Synthetic detergents with branched hydrocarbon chains resist bacterial breakdown, causing persistent foam pollution in natural waterways.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The ester $\text{HCOOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is synthesized by the reaction between
questions.explanation: $\text{HCOOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is ethyl methanoate. Esterification combines an alcohol and a carboxylic acid: methanoic acid ($\text{HCOOH}$) provides the acyl part ($\text{HCO}-$) and ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) provides the alkyl part ($-\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A synthetic polymer used in manufacturing transparent automobile rear light covers and rigid contact lenses is
questions.explanation: Perspex (polymethyl methacrylate, PMMA) is a transparent, shatter-resistant thermoplastic used as a glass substitute in aircraft windows, automobile tail-light covers, and hard contact lenses.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What mass of bromine gas is produced at the anode during the electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide ($\text{PbBr}_2$) when $10.35\ \text{g}$ of lead metal is deposited at the cathode? [$\text{Pb} = 207, \text{Br} = 80$]
questions.explanation: Electrolysis equation: $\text{PbBr}_2(l) \rightarrow \text{Pb}(l) + \text{Br}_2(g)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of a convex polygon with $n$ sides?
questions.explanation: The formula for the sum of interior angles in an $n$-gon is $(n-2) \times 180^\circ$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the value of $\log_{10}(1000)$?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the solution to the equation $2x + 5 = 15$?
questions.explanation: Subtract 5 from both sides ($2x = 10$), then divide by 2 ($x = 5$).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: What is the value of $\sin(\frac{\pi}{6})$?
questions.explanation: $\sin(30^\circ) = \sin(\frac{\pi}{6}) = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The principal turned a deaf ear to the students' complaints. This means that he
questions.explanation: To "turn a deaf ear" to something means to deliberately ignore it or refuse to listen to it — the principal chose not to pay attention to the complaints.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: If a politician sits on the fence, he

options.A: refuses to take a definite position

questions.explanation: Someone who "sits on the fence" avoids committing to either side of an issue — they refuse to take a clear, definite position.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The manager said that the new employee had a chip on his shoulder. This means the employee
questions.explanation: To have "a chip on one's shoulder" means to carry a lingering feeling of resentment or grievance, often over feeling unfairly treated — it describes someone who is unnecessarily resentful, not someone who is injured or generous.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The scientist's explanation left no stone unturned. This means that the scientist
questions.explanation: This idiom means to try every possible way or method to achieve something — it describes a very thorough effort, not carelessness.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The man's audacious behaviour shocked everyone.
questions.explanation: "Audacious" describes behaviour that is bold and daring, often in a way that surprises or shocks others.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The teacher was meticulous in marking the scripts.
questions.explanation: "Meticulous" describes someone who pays very careful, close attention to detail — being thorough rather than careless or quick.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The witness gave a plausible explanation.
questions.explanation: "Plausible" means something seems reasonable or likely to be true — in other words, believable.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The minister's speech was concise.
questions.explanation: "Concise" means expressing something clearly using few words — in other words, brief.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The student's answer was ambiguous.
questions.explanation: "Ambiguous" describes something that can be understood in more than one way, making its meaning unclear.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The government plans to curtail unnecessary expenditure.
questions.explanation: "Curtail" means to cut short or reduce something, especially spending, rights, or activities.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The man's benevolent actions were praised.
questions.explanation: "Benevolent" describes actions or a person that are kind, generous, and well-meaning — in other words, charitable.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The chairman's decision was arbitrary.
questions.explanation: "Arbitrary" means based on random choice or personal whim rather than any reason or system. Its opposite is "systematic," meaning done according to a fixed plan or method.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The witness gave a credible account.
questions.explanation: "Credible" means believable or trustworthy. Its opposite is "doubtful," which suggests something is uncertain or hard to believe.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The medicine had an adverse effect.
questions.explanation: "Adverse" means harmful or unfavourable. Its opposite is "beneficial," meaning helpful or advantageous.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: His argument was coherent.
questions.explanation: "Coherent" describes something that is logical, clear, and easy to follow. Its opposite is "confused," describing something disorganized or hard to understand.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The candidate was reluctant to accept the offer.
questions.explanation: "Reluctant" means unwilling or hesitant to do something. Its opposite is "eager," which means enthusiastic and willing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Neither the students nor their teacher ______ aware of the change.
questions.explanation: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject. The nearer subject here is "teacher," which is singular, so the verb must be singular: "was."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: If I ______ you, I would reconsider the decision.
questions.explanation: This is the subjunctive mood, used for hypothetical or unreal situations. In formal English, "were" is used with "I" in statements like this ("If I were you..."), even though "I" would normally take "was" elsewhere.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: By the time we arrived, the lecture ______.
questions.explanation: The lecture had already started before the group arrived, so the past perfect tense ("had begun") is needed to show that one past action happened before another past action.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The committee ______ divided in its opinion.
questions.explanation: "Committee" is a collective noun. Since the sentence uses the singular possessive "its," the committee is being treated as one single unit here, so it takes the singular verb "is."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: She prefers reading ______ watching television.
questions.explanation: The correct construction is "prefer something TO something else" (not "than"), so "to" is the correct word to complete this comparison.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He has lived in Ibadan ______ 2022.
questions.explanation: "Since" is used with a specific point in time (like a year or date) to show when an ongoing action started. "For" would instead be used to state a duration, such as "for three years."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The students arrived ______ the examination had started.
questions.explanation: The examination had already begun (shown by the past perfect "had started") before the students arrived, so "after" correctly shows that their arrival happened later than the start of the exam.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: I would rather you ______ here tonight.
questions.explanation: After "would rather" when talking about someone else's action, English uses a past tense form even though the meaning is present or future — this subjunctive-like structure makes "stayed" the correct choice here.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The news ______ shocking.
questions.explanation: "News" looks plural because it ends in "-s," but it is grammatically singular, so it takes the singular verb "was."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: One of my friends ______ going to Lagos tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is "one" (singular), not "friends," so the verb must be singular: "is."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Hardly had the teacher entered ______ the students became silent.
questions.explanation: "Hardly...when" is a fixed idiomatic pairing used to show that one event happened immediately after another. It is not paired with "than," which instead pairs with "no sooner."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: No sooner had he arrived ______ it began to rain.
questions.explanation: "No sooner...than" is the fixed idiomatic pairing used to show that one event happened immediately after another.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The woman, together with her children, ______ arrived.
questions.explanation: The main subject of the sentence is "woman" (singular); the phrase "together with her children" is a parenthetical addition and does not change the number of the subject, so the verb stays singular: "has."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In the sentence, "The boy ran quickly," the word "quickly" is a/an
questions.explanation: "Quickly" describes how the boy ran — it modifies the verb "ran" — which is exactly what an adverb does.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In "The book on the table is mine," the expression "on the table" functions as
questions.explanation: "On the table" begins with the preposition "on," followed by its object "the table." A phrase built this way, starting with a preposition, is called a prepositional phrase.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
questions.explanation: When "however" starts a sentence as a linking word meaning "nevertheless," it should be followed by a comma to separate it from the rest of the sentence.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word is correctly spelt?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is "privilege" — note there is no "d" before the "g," unlike the common misspelling "priviledge."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is "accommodation," with two c's and two m's — a commonly misspelled word.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The quality of the products ______ excellent.
questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is "quality" (singular), not "products," so the verb must be singular: "is."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Each of the boys ______ a book.
questions.explanation: "Each" is always treated as singular, even when followed by a plural phrase like "of the boys," so the verb must be singular: "has."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The police ______ investigating the matter.
questions.explanation: "Police" is one of a small group of nouns that are always treated as plural in standard English, so it takes the plural verb "are."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Mathematics ______ one of his favourite subjects.
questions.explanation: Although "Mathematics" ends in "-s," it refers to a single subject and is treated as a singular noun, so it takes the singular verb "is."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The pair of shoes ______ under the bed.
questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is "pair," which is treated as a single unit here, so it takes the singular verb "is."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as "seat."
questions.explanation: "Seat" and "beat" both contain the long vowel sound /iː/. "Sit," "set," and "said" all have different, shorter vowel sounds.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as "cup."
questions.explanation: "Cup" and "luck" both contain the short vowel sound /ʌ/, as in "cut" or "much." The other options have different vowel sounds — "put" and "boot" have rounded vowel sounds, and "food" has a long /uː/ sound.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word has a different vowel sound?
questions.explanation: "Beat," "seat," and "meat" all contain the vowel sound /iː/, but "great" is pronounced with /eɪ/ instead, making it the odd one out.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word rhymes with "light"?
questions.explanation: "Light" is pronounced /laɪt/, and "height" is pronounced /haɪt/ — both share the same ending vowel and consonant sounds, which is what makes them rhyme.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word has the same initial consonant sound as "chair"?
questions.explanation: "Chair" and "church" both begin with the /tʃ/ sound. "Chemist," "character," and "chorus" all begin with a /k/ sound instead, even though they're all spelled with "ch."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word contains a silent "k"?
questions.explanation: In English, the letter "k" is silent when it comes before "n" at the start of a word, as in "knee," "knife," and "know." In "king," "keep," and "kind," the "k" is pronounced normally.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word has the stress on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: "Relax" is stressed on its second syllable (re-LAX). "Table," "doctor," and "present" (as used here) are all stressed on their first syllable.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word has the stress on the first syllable?
questions.explanation: "Teacher" is stressed on its first syllable (TEACH-er). "Begin," "about," and "allow" are all stressed on their second syllable instead.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word has a different consonant sound for the underlined letter combination "ch"?
questions.explanation: "Ch" in "machine" is pronounced /ʃ/, unlike the /tʃ/ sound heard in "chair," "church," and "child."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which word contains the /θ/ sound?
questions.explanation: "Thin" contains the unvoiced "th" sound /θ/, as in "think" or "three." "Then," "this," and "those" all contain the voiced "th" sound /ð/ instead.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The expression "to spill the beans" means to
questions.explanation: "To spill the beans" means to reveal secret or private information, often accidentally or before it was meant to be known.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: If someone "hit the nail on the head," the person
questions.explanation: This idiom describes doing or saying something with complete accuracy, getting to the exact point of a matter — much like a hammer striking a nail precisely on its head.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The expression "once in a blue moon" means
questions.explanation: "Once in a blue moon" describes something that happens very rarely or almost never, since a "blue moon" — a second full moon in one calendar month — is itself an uncommon event.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The student's success was attributed to hard work. The expression means that his success was
questions.explanation: To say something is "attributed to" a cause means that cause is credited with being responsible for it — his success was said to be the result of his hard work.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The sentence "The manager had the report typed" means that

options.A: the manager typed the report personally
options.B: someone typed the report for the manager
options.D: the manager refused to type the report

questions.explanation: This is the causative structure "have + object + past participle." "Had the report typed" means the manager arranged for somebody else to type it, not that he typed it himself.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What usually opens the morning assembly in the school?

options.C: The second stanza of the national anthem

questions.explanation: In The Lekki Headmaster, the morning assembly typically begins with Christian and Muslim prayers.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: How much money was involved in the financial issue mentioned?

options.A: one hundred and sixty three thousand naira
options.B: two hundred and fifty thousand naira
options.C: one hundred and sixty thousand naira

questions.explanation: The amount referenced in the novel context is two hundred and fifty thousand naira.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Who is the highest authority figure referred to in the school?
questions.explanation: The Managing Director holds the highest administrative authority in the school setting of the novel.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Why was an emergency meeting summoned?

options.B: Because parents were calling with concerns

questions.explanation: The emergency meeting was called due to numerous calls from concerned parents.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Why was the headmaster nicknamed in connection with “Lekki Headmaster”?

options.A: He lived in Lekki during his time as a headmaster
options.B: He humorously imitated characters from the Village Headmaster
options.C: He introduced a new curriculum in the school

questions.explanation: The nickname arose from his humorous imitation of characters from the classic Village Headmaster series.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Each of the answers ______ correct.
questions.explanation: "Each" is singular, so the verb must be singular "is".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Each of the reports ______ been carefully reviewed by the committee.
questions.explanation: "Each" takes a singular verb; the correct form is "has been".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The ____ of armed robbery has been on the increase.
questions.explanation: "Incidence" means the rate or frequency of occurrence of something.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The doctor ____ him to take his medicine regularly.
questions.explanation: The correct past tense of the verb "advise" is "advised". "Advice" is a noun.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The teacher insisted that the students ______ talking.
questions.explanation: After verbs like "insist that", the subjunctive mood is used: base form of the verb "stop".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correct order of adjectives:
questions.explanation: The correct order of adjectives is opinion/size/age/shape/colour/origin/material/purpose. "Shiny new red lunch" follows this.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The journey was ______ long for the children.
questions.explanation: "Too" is used to indicate excessiveness: "too long".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: I have not seen him ______ last week.
questions.explanation: "Since" is used with a specific point in time (last week).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: If he had studied harder, he ______ higher marks.
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional sentence: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: It’s a beautiful day, ______?
questions.explanation: The statement is present tense positive, so the tag question is negative present: "isn’t it?"

questions.subject: English
questions.question: A ______ of sheep was grazing on the hill.
questions.explanation: The collective noun for sheep is "flock".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: She has been ______ a reply from the company for weeks.
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is "waiting for a reply".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Neither of the boys ______ completed the assignment.
questions.explanation: "Neither" is singular and takes a singular verb "has".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He rarely comes late, ______?
questions.explanation: "Rarely" makes the statement negative in meaning, so the tag is positive: "didn’t he?" is incorrect; wait — actually for negative adverbs the tag is affirmative. Correct is "does he?" but among options the closest standard is D in many keys; standard is affirmative tag.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The committee ______ divided in their opinion.
questions.explanation: When the committee members are acting individually (divided opinions), plural verb "are" is used.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: I prefer tea ______ coffee.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition after "prefer" is "to".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The man, as well as his children, ______ present.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the first subject "the man" (singular).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: She is one of those who ______ always complaining.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun "who" refers to "those" (plural), so "are".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: By this time next year, I ______ my degree.
questions.explanation: Future perfect tense is used for an action that will be completed by a certain future time.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He talks as if he ______ everything.
questions.explanation: "As if" is followed by the past subjunctive for unreal present situations.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Neither John nor his friends ______ available.
questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject ("friends" – plural).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The number of students ______ increasing every year.
questions.explanation: "The number of" takes a singular verb.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: She has been living here ______ 2018.
questions.explanation: "Since" is used with a specific point in time.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He got a job by paying hush money.

options.A: He bribed to get the job
options.B: He was induced to get the job
options.C: He paid exorbitant fee to get the job
options.D: He was paid for the job

questions.explanation: "Hush money" means a bribe paid to keep someone silent or to secure a favour.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The chairman told members not to throw in the towel.

options.B: They are not to give up
options.C: They should be ready for a trip

questions.explanation: "Throw in the towel" is an idiom meaning to give up or surrender.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Despite his wealth, Mr Oluboye is known for tightening his belt.

options.B: He is very careful with his spending
options.C: He refuses to wear a belt at all

questions.explanation: "Tighten one’s belt" means to spend less money or live more frugally.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The excuses are full of holes.

options.A: The excuses are not logically sound
options.B: The excuses are acceptable by a few
options.D: The excuses explain the situation well

questions.explanation: "Full of holes" means full of flaws or not convincing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to rigid:
questions.explanation: "Rigid" means stiff or inflexible; "unbendable" is the closest synonym.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to available:
questions.explanation: The word itself is already the correct option in the original set; nearest among others is functional in some contexts, but A is direct.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to enemy:
questions.explanation: "Antagonist" is a close synonym of enemy, especially in literary contexts.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to impermeable:
questions.explanation: "Pervious" means allowing passage; opposite of impermeable.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The students were asked to ______ their essays carefully.
questions.explanation: The correct adjective is "careful".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The king was ______ after the rebellion.
questions.explanation: "Dethroned" means removed from the throne.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: She has a ______ knowledge of the subject.
questions.explanation: "Broad knowledge" is the correct collocation meaning extensive knowledge.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The foreigners were regarded as ______.
questions.explanation: In the context of the options, "immigrants" fits best for people who have moved into the country.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He tried to ______ the angry crowd.
questions.explanation: "Appease" means to calm or pacify.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The politician was ______ for his corrupt practices.
questions.explanation: "Denounced" means publicly condemned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The matter requires ______ attention.
questions.explanation: "Careful attention" is the appropriate collocation.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The Security ______ has a primary responsibility for the maintenance of international ______.
questions.explanation: It is the UN Security Council that has primary responsibility for international peace and security.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: ... peace and ______.
questions.explanation: The standard phrase is "international peace and security".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: It has fifteen ______.
questions.explanation: The Security Council has fifteen members.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Each Member has one ______.
questions.explanation: Each member of the Security Council has one vote.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Under the ______, all Member States are obligated...
questions.explanation: The UN Charter is the founding document.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: ... existence of a ______ to the peace.
questions.explanation: The standard term is "threat to the peace".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: It calls upon the ______ to a dispute...
questions.explanation: "Parties to a dispute" is the correct legal term.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: ... methods of ______.
questions.explanation: "Methods of settlement" or "peaceful settlement of disputes".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: ... imposing ______ or even authorise the use of force.
questions.explanation: The Security Council can impose sanctions.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In formal official language, “red tape” means:

options.B: Red tape worm is found everywhere

questions.explanation: "Red tape" refers to excessive bureaucracy or official formality.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which register is most appropriate for a formal letter of application?
questions.explanation: Formal letters require formal and polite language.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: “Japa” in contemporary Nigerian English most nearly means:

options.B: To travel abroad in search of better opportunities
options.D: To work as a slave in a foreign country

questions.explanation: "Japa" is a popular Nigerian slang meaning to emigrate or flee abroad for better opportunities.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The expression “brain drain” refers to:

options.A: Loss of skilled professionals to other countries

questions.explanation: Brain drain is the emigration of highly trained or qualified people from a particular country.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In a formal meeting, the correct way to address the chairman is:
questions.explanation: The formal and correct form of address is "Mr Chairman" or "Madam Chair".
